The Estrobolome
Think of your gut and your hormones like two best friends at brunch: they are
constantly gossiping about you behind your back, and if one of them is having a bad
day, everyone is going to hear about it. (ﾟωﾟ；) Your gut is not just handling
digestion. It is also involved in inflammation, immune signaling, metabolism, nutrient
processing, and even the way certain hormones are activated and cleared. So when
the gut feels off, hormones can follow suit.


Now, this does not mean every hormone problem begins in the gut, and it definitely
does not mean a cup of yogurt alone is going to solve all of your endocrine-related
issues. But it does mean the gut can meaningfully influence hormonal balance,
especially when it comes to estrogen metabolism, insulin sensitivity, inflammation,
and reproductive health.


As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. If you are
dealing with severe digestive symptoms, missed periods, suspected PCOS,
endometriosis, infertility, or major hormone-related changes, it is important to
work with a qualified clinician.

125


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

The gut and the hormone system work hand in hand. Hormones can shape the gut
environment, and the gut microbiome can shape how hormones are processed and
recycled. It truly is a two-way street! ദ്ദി ( ᵔ ᗜ ᵔ ) Once you wrap your mind around
that little back-and-forth, the whole “gut         health and hormone balance”
conversation starts feeling much more approachable, and much less fluffy.


☆ The Gut Microbiome Is Doing More Than Digestion
      ​The gut microbiome refers to the community of bacteria and other
      microbes living in the digestive tract.
            ​These microbes help with digestion, metabolism, immune regulation,
             inflammation, gut barrier integrity, and the production of signaling
             molecules.
                  ​Because all of those systems interact with hormones, the gut
                   has a crucial impact on endocrine function. So, no, it’s not some
                   forgettable side character. It’s very much part of the main
                   plot!


      ☆ The Estrobolome Is One Of The Key Links
            ​The estrobolome is the collection of gut bacterial genes involved in
             estrogen metabolism.
                  ​One of the main players is an enzyme called beta-glucuronidase
                   (β-Glucuronidase).
                           ​This enzyme helps deconjugate, or reactivate (in plain
                           English), estrogens that were excreted into the gut.
                                 ​Once reactivated, some of those estrogens can be
                                 reabsorbed into circulation.


So, in other words, the gut can partly influence how much active estrogen stays in
play in the body! Pretty cool, huh? ☆⌒(ゝ。∂)


☆ So, What Happens When The Gut Is Unbalanced?

126

      ​Well … let’s just say that it wouldn’t be a good day for your hormones.
      (⊙ _ ⊙ ) As previously mentioned, estrogen doesn’t just float around all
      willy-nilly in your body. When gut microbial diversity drops, a state often
      called dysbiosis, estrobolome function may become less stable.
           ​Lower β-Glucuronidase activity leads to more estrogen being
            excreted rather than recycled.
                 ​That may contribute to lower active estrogen levels or altered
                  estrogen metabolism.


      ☆ The Relationship Goes Both Ways (It’s A Feedback Loop)
           ​Sex hormones also shape the gut microbiome.
                 ​Estrogen,    progesterone,       and   androgens   can   influence
                  microbiome composition, function, and diversity.
                        ​Hormonal changes across the menstrual cycle, pregnancy,
                         perimenopause, and menopause can all shift the gut
                         environment.
           ​Those shifts may favor some bacteria and disadvantage others.


            ☆ Menopause Is One Of The Clearest Examples
                 ​Menopause has been associated with lower microbial diversity.
                        ​It has also been linked with a shift toward a more
                         male-typical gut microbiome composition (｡ᵕ °ㅁ° ).
                        ​Beneficial     bacteria    such   as   Lactobacillus   and
                         Bifidobacteria may decline.
                              ​Reduced microbial diversity during this transition
                               may worsen metabolic changes, estrogen-related
                               symptoms,     and overall resilience. That helps
                               explain why hormonal transitions can feel so
                               full-body.


      ☆ Gut Bacteria Affect Metabolism And Inflammation Too
           ​Gut microbes produce short-chain fatty acids, bile acid metabolites,
            and other signaling molecules!

127

                  ​These molecules influence metabolism, insulin sensitivity,
                    immune regulation, and inflammatory tone.
                         ​Those systems then affect hormone pathways, including
                          insulin-related signaling and broader endocrine balance.
                          As you can see, this can all create a bit of a domino
                          effect. ( ' ﹋ ' ; )
            ​The gut is also involved in maintaining the intestinal barrier, which
             helps regulate what passes into circulation.


Hormones do not operate in a vacuum. They are influenced by the body’s
inflammatory state, metabolic health, and immune signaling too!


☆ Why “Leaky Gut” And Low-Grade Inflammation Matter
      ​Dysbiosis can weaken gut barrier integrity.
            ​When that happens, inflammatory compounds and endotoxins may
             move more easily into circulation.
            ​This can promote low-grade chronic inflammation.
                  ​Chronic inflammation can disrupt endocrine signaling, including
                    communication along the hypothalamic-pituitary axes that help
                    regulate the body.


      It goes beyond bloating & digestion. The whole system gets thrown off
      balance, becoming more inflamed and more unstable.


☆ Reproductive And Ovarian Health Are Connected Too


      ​Animal and human studies have linked gut microbiota profiles with
      reproductive hormone levels and ovarian function. Certain bacterial patterns
      have been associated with insulin, testosterone, LH, FSH, and ovarian
      morphology.
            ​Gut microbiota differences have also been linked with conditions such
             as PCOS, endometriosis, and infertility.

128

                  ​Fun fact: in experimental models, transferring gut microbiota
                   from individuals with PCOS into mice produced both metabolic
                   and reproductive dysfunction in the animals that received it.


      ☆ What This Can Look Like In Real Life
            ​Women with gut dysbiosis from poor diet, repeated antibiotics,
            chronic GI conditions, or other disruptions may be more prone to
            hormonal irregularities.
                  ​That can show up as erratic cycles, estrogen-withdrawal-like
                   symptoms, insulin resistance, or a general sense that things feel
                   hormonally unstable.
                  ​During perimenopause and menopause, gut changes may worsen
                   hot flashes, metabolic shifts, and estrogen-related symptoms.
            ​The gut may also influence how resilient the body feels during times
            of major hormonal change.


It’s important to note that this does not mean every hormone issue is secretly a
gut issue. It simply means gut health is one meaningful piece of the larger picture,
especially when symptoms cluster with digestive issues, inflammation, or metabolic
changes. Now that we’ve unpacked how this connection works, let’s get into what
can actually help support it in everyday life.

Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

The gut-hormone connection is such a good reminder that the body works in
relationships, not in isolated little boxes. The gut can influence estrogen
metabolism, inflammation, insulin sensitivity, immune balance, and even aspects of
reproductive function, while hormones also shape the gut environment in return.
That means caring for your gut may help support hormonal steadiness in a very
real, very physiological way. The most helpful place to begin is simple: feed the
good bacteria, lower unnecessary inflammatory stress, and work with your body
consistently enough that it has a chance to feel more resilient!

Self-Care Routines
There is such a difference between self-care that belongs on a Pinterest board,
and self-care that actually supports you. The second kind is the one that lingers.
It shows up in how your skin feels after you moisturize it properly, how your scalp
behaves when it is consistently cared for, how your body softens when your routine
is less irritating, and how much calmer everything feels when your rituals actually
match your needs. Now, that is the kind of care this section is about. (づ> v <)づ♡


Women's beauty and wellness are rarely treated like separate worlds. Skin care
overlaps with barrier repair. Hair care overlaps with scalp remedies. Fragrance
overlaps with mood, ritual, and emotional regulation. Intimate care overlaps with
microbiome support and restraint. And herbal ingredients are often doing more
than one job at once. They moisturize, calm, cleanse, cool, soften, strengthen,
brighten, restore, and protect!


As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. Patch testing
matters! Menopause, eczema-prone skin, fragrance allergies, and intimate-area
care all require extra attention. Natural does not automatically mean safe.

☆ Intimate Care Basics
      ​For all women! Especially those who are: sensitive, irritation-prone,
      fragrance-reactive, BV-prone, post-antibiotic, or generally cautious routines.
               ​External cleansing only.
               ​Gentle fragrance-free product if needed.
               ​Breathable cotton underwear.
               ​Hydration.
               ​Low-irritation habits.
               ​Oral probiotics with Lactobacillus rhamnosus GR-1 and Lactobacillus
               reuteri RC-14 if useful.
                     ​Yogurt with live cultures, kefir, kimchi, sauerkraut, miso,
                      tempeh + fiber-rich foods.


                             Avoid:
                                   ​Douching.
                                   ​Perfumed vaginal products.
                                   ​Scented yoni bars.
                                   ​Harsh soaps.
                                   ​Essential oils on intimate tissue.
                                   ​Exfoliating acids on vulvar skin.

            ☆ If Shaving:
                  ​Use warm water.
                  ​Use a clean, sharp razor.
                  ​Use shaving gel or cream for slip.
                  ​Shave    gently,    ideally   with the direction of growth if
                   ingrown-prone.
                  ​Follow with aloe vera or fragrance-free moisturizer.
                  ​Use     chemical    exfoliation   only    on   non-shave   days   if

                         ​Avoid:
                                ​Dull razors.
                                ​Dry shaving.
                                ​Strong fragrance right after.
                                ​Broken or freshly exfoliated skin.
                                ​Aggressive scrubbing.


            ☆ If Chemical Depilatory:
                  ​Patch test first.
                  ​Use only on intact, non-irritated skin.
                  ​Keep it to less-sensitive body areas unless face-safe and
                   personally tolerated.
                  ​Moisturize simply afterward.
                         ​Avoid:
                                ​Leaving it on too long.

                          ​Using it too close to acids, retinoids, or strong
                           exfoliation.


      ☆ If Plucking / Threading:
           ​Keep it to small areas.
           ​Warm skin first.
           ​Use clean tools or a trusted practitioner.
           ​Follow with aloe vera or bland calming moisturizer.
                 ​Avoid:
                          ​Dirty tweezers.
                          ​Repeated picking.
                          ​Large-area plucking.
                          ​Strong actives right before or after (let your skin
                           breathe :-) ).


      ☆ If Waxing / Sugaring:
           ​Make sure hair is long enough.
           ​Keep skin calm before.
           ​Use fragrance-free soothing care afterward.
           ​Wear loose clothing after bikini / body waxing.
           ​Pause strong actives around facial waxing.
                 ​Avoid:
                          ​Irritated, sunburned, or broken skin.
                          ​Systemic retinoids.
                          ​Ultra-short stubble.
                          ​Aggressive exfoliation too close together.


      ☆ If Laser / IPL:
           ​Shave beforehand.
           ​Do not wax or pluck before treatment.
           ​Avoid tanning.

Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

The richest self-care routines are not the ones with the most pretty products.
They are the ones with the most thought behind them. When you bring together
barrier-friendly moisture, scalp-first care, microbiome respect, calming herbs,
thoughtful fragrance, and routines that match your actual body, self-care stops
feeling performative and starts feeling restorative. So, no, you don’t have to do
the most. Never that. It all boils down to doing what pairs well, what makes sense,
and what lets your body feel beautifully supported over time. <𝟑 .ᐟ

Body Image & Beauty S tandards
It is honestly so easy for women to feel watched, measured, compared, and edited
behind the scenes at all times. Your body can be perfectly normal, healthy, and
human, and still somehow feel “wrong” under enough pressure. This does not mean
you are vain. It means you are living in a world that teaches women to over-monitor
themselves. And, apparently, we’re supposed to keep it all together, look radiant,
and somehow not break a sweat. Like sure… let me just grab my superheroine cape
and save the world real quick. (￣へ￣)

Body image and self-esteem aren’t random, either. They are shaped by hormones,
brain chemistry, life experiences, family messages, social media, culture, and the
way you have learned to speak to yourself over time. The good news is that neither
one is fixed. Both can be softened, rebuilt, and strengthened with practice.

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. If body image
struggles are severe, persistent, or tied to disordered eating, depression, or
strong avoidance behaviors, professional support really matters.

176


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Sometimes the most healing thing is realizing that body image struggles are not
proof that something is wrong with you. I mean, your mind may be talking up a
storm, but that’s not on you. (o´・ω・)ノ(ノω・。) Body image struggles are often a
very understandable response to pressure, change, and emotional pain. Once you
understand what is shaping the way you see yourself, it becomes much easier to
answer with care instead of guilt!

☆ What Body Image And Self-Esteem Actually Are
      ​Body image is how you think and feel about your body, how you perceive it,
      and how you treat it.
      ​Self-esteem is the broader way you value yourself overall.
            ​The two overlap, but they are not identical.
      ​A woman can feel confident in some areas of life and still struggle deeply
      with appearance.
            ​And even that confidence may fall to the wayside at times! ( : ౦ ‸ ౦ : )
                  ​A woman can also notice her body image shifting with stress,
                   hormones, relationships, life transitions, or the environment she
                   is in.

      So, it is important to try to remember that you are worth far more than
      what is on the surface. Body image is one part of your internal world. It is
      not your whole identity.

Now, negative body image is not just about “confidence.” It is often tied to the way
the brain, body, and environment are interacting. This is why telling a woman to
“just love herself” can feel so hollow and ineffective sometimes. The issue is often
deeper than one mindset quote and a cutesy mirror affirmation. (ᵕ—ᴗ—)
      ​Body image and self-esteem are shaped by biological, psychological, and
      sociocultural factors.
            ​Hormonal shifts, stress, low mood, trauma, criticism, and comparison
             can all intensify body dissatisfaction.

177

            ​Brain regions that may be involved in self-perception and emotional
             evaluation, such as the insula and amygdala, can become more reactive
             in people struggling with body dissatisfaction.
            ​Low serotonin, chronic stress, and emotional overload can intensify
             harsh self-talk about appearance.


☆ Hormones And Body Image Across A Woman’s Life
      ​The menstrual cycle can affect mood, sensitivity, and body satisfaction.
      ​During the follicular phase, rising estrogen may support better mood and
      slightly better body image.
      ​Around ovulation, peak estrogen and testosterone may temporarily increase
      confidence.
      ​During the luteal     phase, rising progesterone and greater emotional
      sensitivity may increase bloating, insecurity, self-criticism, and body
      dissatisfaction.
            ​Pregnancy and postpartum can bring rapid body changes, hormonal
             shifts, and appearance-related anxiety.
            ​Many postpartum women (around 60%) report negative feelings about
             appearance as their bodies recover and adjust after birth.
            ​Perimenopause and menopause can also affect self-esteem through
             changes in skin elasticity, body composition, fat distribution, and
             energy.
                    ​Of course, this doesn’t mean hormones cause all insecurity, but
                    they definitely can influence how strong body dissatisfaction
                    feels.

This is why cycle tracking can come to your rescue! (ง˃ ᴗ ˂)ง Sometimes your body
is moving through a more sensitive window, and your mind may simply need a little
extra kindness to catch up before it feels steady again.

☆ Social Media And Comparison Pressure
      ​Social media exposure can worsen body dissatisfaction, self-objectification,
      shame, and comparison.

178

             ​Seeing idealized bodies over and over again can make unrealistic
                appearance standards feel normal.
             ​Content built around the ‘perfect’ body, whether that means thin,
                toned, curvy, or “slim thick,” can distort self-perception.
                     ​Media literacy matters because many images are filtered,
                      edited, posed, or chosen from hundreds of attempts!
                            ​Reducing triggering exposure, unfollowing accounts that
                             make you feel chronically inadequate, and limiting time on
                             appearance-heavy platforms can help.

One very practical guideline here is to be intentional about what you keep looking
at. Sometimes, it really is that damn phone. Your nervous system doesn’t need a
daily buffet of reasons to feel insufficient. So, please, try not to rub salt into your
wounds! ♡(˃͈ ˂͈ )

☆ Family, Peers, And Cultural Messaging
      ​Negative comments about weight, shape, beauty, or dieting during
       adolescence can leave long-lasting effects on self-esteem.
      ​Family and peer messages often become the inner voice women carry for
       years.
      ​Beauty standards also change across cultures, which can create confusion
       and pressure.
             ​Some cultures glorify thinness.
             ​Some glorify curviness.
             ​Some glorify youthfulness, softness, or constant effortlessness.
             ​Understanding that beauty standards are socially shaped can help
                weaken their influence.

                So take a breath! Your outer world plays a big role in your inner one. A
                lot of what women think is personal failure is often just social
                conditioning wearing a very convincing outfit. (^_−)☆

179

So, how do you know if you may be struggling with body image or self-worth? Well,
there are a few patterns to look out for. Please keep in mind that if any of these
hit close to home, it does not make you shallow. It makes you human and, very
possibly, tired. (T～T；。) Tangent aside, let’s take a look a few clues:
      ​Constant body-checking.
      ​Mirror avoidance or mirror distress.
      ​Frequent comparison.
      ​Feeling “not enough” no matter what you accomplish.
      ​Harsh self-talk.
      ​Avoiding certain clothes, events, photos, or intimacy because of appearance
      shame.
      ​Feeling disconnected from yourself.
      ​Needing constant validation to feel okay.
      ​Exhaustion from always trying to be more attractive, more acceptable, or
      less visible.
      ​Persistent insecurity that affects eating, movement, relationships, or mental
      health.

Okay, now let’s delve into the concept of self-love. There is a much gentler and
more realistic definition than the internet usually gives. It is not “I think I am
gorgeous every second.” Sometimes it is simply, “I will not bully myself today.”
      ​It is not vanity, selfishness, or ego.
      ​It is having a healthy, kind, respectful relationship with yourself.
            ​It includes acceptance, compassion, boundaries, forgiveness, honesty,
             and care.
            ​It affects how you speak to yourself, what you tolerate, what
             relationships you choose, and how you recover from hard things.
            ​It is not pretending you feel amazing all the time. Instead, it is
             refusing to abandon yourself, even on hard days.


☆ The First Step: Awaken To Yourself
      ​Self-love often begins with a moment of waking up.
            ​You realize that approval is not peace.
            ​You realize that perfection is not safety.

180

            ​You realize that hating yourself is not making you better.
      ​This awakening may come through heartbreak, burnout, loss, therapy,
      motherhood, illness, disappointment, or plain emotional exhaustion.
            ​Awareness comes before change! (◠ ‿ ◠)

Transformation requires friction. A lot of women begin loving themselves not
because life was easy, but because they got tired of being cruel to themselves
and realized it was not working.

☆ CBT-Style Body Image Tools
      ​Notice body-negative thoughts as they happen.
      ​Name them clearly.
      ​Ask whether they are factual, helpful, and kind.
      ​Replace them with more neutral, grounded statements.
            ​E.g., instead of “I look disgusting,” try “I am feeling uncomfortable in
             my body right now, and that feeling is real, but it is not the full truth
             about me.”
                   ​Instead of “I am too fat to be seen,” try “My body is allowed to
                   exist as it is today.”
      ​Behavioral experiments can also help.
            ​Wear clothes that actually fit.
            ​Notice how you feel in supportive clothing versus punishing clothing.
            ​Observe the shift in self-perception.

This work can feel awkward at first, but it is impactful! Your brain learns through
repetition. If you keep interrupting self-deprecation, you slowly stop giving it the
only microphone in the room.

☆ Mindfulness And Self-Compassion
      ​Mindfulness helps you notice thoughts without instantly becoming them.
      ​Self-compassion helps you respond to yourself with care instead of
      contempt.
      ​Daily practices can include meditation, breathwork, stretching, quiet sitting,
      or journaling.

181

            ​A gentle journaling prompt is: “Name three things my body did for me
             today.”
            ​Another is: “What do I need right now that has nothing to do with
             being prettier?”
      ​Self-compassion reminders can include:
            ​Healing is not linear.
            ​Mistakes do not erase worth.
            ​Having needs does not make me weak.
            ​I can struggle and still be worthy.

☆ Mirror Anxiety And Body Avoidance
      ​Mirror anxiety can improve through gradual exposure.
            ​Instead of obsessively scanning or avoiding mirrors completely,
             practice calmer, more neutral observation.
            ​Focus on the whole body rather than picking apart one area.
            ​Focus on function, presence, and neutrality before trying to force
             admiration.
      ​Keep mirror time intentional, not compulsive.
      ​Clothes that fit now, not “goal clothes,” usually help reduce body-checking
      distress.

In this case, the goal is not to stare at yourself until you suddenly feel beautiful.
Instead, the goal is to build a less hostile relationship with your reflection! ^___^

☆ Exercise For Function, Not Punishment
      ​Exercise can support body appreciation when it is rooted in function rather
      than self-hatred.
            ​Weight lifting 2 to 3 times weekly may improve mood, body
             appreciation, and bone health.
            ​Yoga and Pilates can improve mind-body awareness and reduce stress.
      ​Supportive movement helps most when it is framed around strength, energy,
      mobility, steadiness, or emotional relief.
      ​Hardcore, punishing exercise usually makes body resentment worse.

182

At the end of the day, it’s all about the mindset! “Exercise because I hate my
body” feels very different from “exercise because I want to feel stronger and
more supported inside it.” (⌒▽⌒)☆

☆ Nourishment And Balanced Eating
       ​Extreme dieting often worsens body obsession, mood instability, and shame.
       ​Balanced eating supports mood, energy, and cognitive steadiness.
             ​Protein, fiber, iron, vitamin D, omega-3s, and adequate overall
              nourishment can support mental health indirectly.
       ​Restriction, binge cycles, and chronic guilt around food usually deepen body
       distress rather than healing it.
             ​If eating feels emotionally loaded, professional support can be very
              helpful.

☆ Sleep, Stress, And Emotional Load
       ​7 to 9 hours of sleep can support mood and reduce stress reactivity.
       ​Poor sleep increases cortisol and can intensify emotional sensitivity,
       self-criticism, and body dissatisfaction.
       ​Ongoing stress can also make appearance concerns feel much louder.
             ​Journaling, therapy, stretching, breathwork, supportive routines, and
              reducing overload can all help.

Sometimes the most “body image” problem is actually an exhaustion problem.
(＿ ＿*) Z z z So, please try to give your mind a break; it will take better care of
you.

☆ Practical Ways To Protect Your Self-Esteem
       ​Reduce time with content that makes you feel chronically inadequate.
       ​Unfollow accounts that trigger shame, comparison, or self-objectification.
       ​Choose clothes that fit your current body.
       ​Stop using humiliation as motivation.
       ​Speak to your body with respect, even when you feel insecure.
       ​Spend more time around people who do not make your appearance the price
       of belonging.

183

      ​Build daily rituals that make you grounded, not constantly evaluated.

      ☆ Boundaries As Self-Love
            ​Boundaries are one of the clearest forms of self-respect.
            ​They can sound like:
                   ​“No.”
                   ​“That does not work for me.”
                   ​“I need time.”
                   ​“Please do not speak to me that way.”
                   ​“I am not available for that.”
            ​Setting boundaries can feel guilty at first, especially for women who
             were taught to stay agreeable, over-give, or make themselves easy to
             manage.
            ​Guilt does not always mean you are doing something wrong. Sometimes
             it means you are doing something new.

      ☆ Protecting Your Energy
            ​Notice what drains you.
            ​This may include people, content, environments, conversations, habits,
             or expectations.
            ​Spend less time where you feel inferior, judged, anxious, unseen, or
             emotionally used.
            ​Spend more time where you feel calm, respected, nourished, and safe.
            ​Self-esteem grows better in environments where you are not
             constantly bracing.

      ☆ Inner Child Healing
            ​Many body image wounds and self-worth struggles are tied to earlier
             experiences of criticism, rejection, abandonment, or pressure.
            ​Inner child work can involve journaling to your younger self,
             identifying what she needed, and offering that care now. (´ ω `♡)
            ​Helpful phrases may include:
                   ​“You did not deserve that.”
                   ​“You are safe with me now.”

184

                  ​“You do not have to earn love.”
                  ​“I will not abandon you.”
           ​This kind of work can feel very tender, but very healing.

      A lot of women soften when they realize they have been using adult language
      to bully a younger wound. (っ◞‸◟ c)

      ☆ Building Self-Trust
           ​Self-love is not only about liking yourself. It is also about trusting
            yourself.
           ​Self-trust grows when you keep promises to yourself, listen to your
            feelings, and stop constantly overriding your needs.
           ​Start very small:
                  ​Eat when hungry.
                  ​Go to bed on time.
                  ​Leave situations that feel wrong.
                  ​Follow through on one supportive action each day!

      ☆ Making Self-Care Real, Not Performative
           ​As mentioned in the previous section, real self-care is not just
            candles, facials, and things that look good online.
                  ​Sometimes self-care is therapy.
                  ​Sometimes it is rest.
                  ​Sometimes it is taking your medicine.
                  ​Sometimes it is asking for help.

actually practice. Here are some examples:

      ​Quiet tea time.

      ​Gratitude.

      ​Celebrating small wins.

them! You will likely still have days where you compare yourself, doubt yourself, or
want outside validation. That does not mean you failed. Something very important
to keep in mind is: you do not have to feel amazing about yourself to treat
yourself with dignity.
      ​On hard days, lower the goal.

            ​Try: “I will not abandon myself today.”

Healing body image and self-esteem is usually not about becoming prettier, more
perfect, or more approved of. It is about becoming less cruel to yourself, less
easily manipulated by pressure, and more rooted in your own humanity. The real
shift happens when you stop treating yourself like a problem to solve and start
treating yourself like someone worth protecting, understanding, and loving. Now,
that is where self-esteem gets steadier. And, simultaneously, that is also where

Environmental Toxins (EDCs)
Just when you think you’ve finally cracked the code on women’s health,
environmental toxins show up uninvited like a relative who just will not leave
(｀△´＋). Plastics, receipts, cookware, dust, air pollution, old pipes, certain
cosmetics, and even the air near busy roads can all become part of the
conversation. While it may seem like hazards are lurking in every corner of this
planet, you do not need to panic nor try to live in a glass bubble.

The real objective here is not fear. Not in the slightest! It is awareness, then
gentle strategy. Many environmental toxins are linked to hormone disruption,
fertility issues, menstrual changes, pregnancy complications, and long-term health
effects, but exposure science is complex. Timing, dose, duration, mixtures, and life
stage all play a role. Correlation does not equal causation, and one or two
exposures could be nothing but a storm inside of a teacup. (^_−)☆

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice, and the most
helpful mindset is: reduce what you reasonably can, without spiraling into paranoia.

190


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Now, a good way to think about environmental toxins is not, “How do I remove
every single risk from my life?” but, “Which routine exposure points should I swap
first for maximum protection?” That question keeps this practical instead of
overwhelming.


      ☆ What These Toxins Are And Why Women Should Care
           ​A major group of concern is endocrine-disrupting chemicals, often
            shortened to EDCs.
                  ​These are chemicals that can interfere with hormones by
                  mimicking them, blocking them, or changing how hormone signals
                  work.
                          ​They may affect estrogen, androgen, thyroid, and other
                          hormone pathways.
           ​Women’s health is especially sensitive to this because hormones help
            regulate ovulation, menstrual cycles, fertility, pregnancy, puberty,
            and menopause.
           ​Critical windows matter a lot, especially puberty, pregnancy, fetal
            development, and follicle development in the ovaries.

      This is why the topic matters so much for women specifically! Hormone
      signaling is not peripheral. It is woven through everything. (x_x)⌒☆

      ☆ The Main Ways Toxins Can Affect The Body
           ​Hormone receptor interference means a chemical can act a little like
            estrogen or block normal hormone signaling.
                  ​Epigenetic changes means certain exposures may affect how
                  genes are turned on or off, including in eggs, sperm, embryos, or
                  developing babies.
                          ​Oxidative stress and inflammation can damage tissues,
                          impair placental function, and affect fetal growth.

191

              ​Mixture effects matter too, because in real life we are usually
              exposed to many low-level things together, not one majorly
              detrimental chemical at a time.

Now that we’ve covered how they can affect the body, we can now focus on the
major toxins. Of course, you do not need to memorize every acronym like it is
finals week. ( ᵔ‿ ᵔ “) What matters most is learning the everyday sources and the
easiest swaps!

      ☆ Bisphenols, including BPA, are used in some plastics, can linings, thermal
      paper receipts, and some medical products.

      ☆ Some pesticides can act like endocrine disruptors and may show up

      ☆ PCBs were banned decades ago in the United States, but they persist in

      ☆ PBDEs are flame retardants found in older foam furniture, carpets,

      ☆ PFAS, often called forever chemicals, are found in some non-stick

      ☆ Air pollution includes particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, and ozone,

The strongest takeaway of this section is not that everything is dangerous! It is
that women’s bodies are not overreacting when they are sensitive to hormonal
disruption. With that being said, the most concerning women’s-health outcomes
are:
       ​Reduced fertility or longer time to conception.
             ​Menstrual irregularities and possible disruption of ovulation.
                    ​Possible links to endometriosis, PCOS, uterine fibroids, and

             ​Fetal and child neurodevelopment concerns.

             ​Pregnant women and fetuses are especially vulnerable because
              development happens in very sensitive windows.
                    ​Adolescents   are   vulnerable    because   puberty   is   heavily
                    hormone-dependent.
                    ​Women trying to conceive may be especially motivated to
                    reduce avoidable exposures.
                    ​Communities of color and socioeconomically disadvantaged
                    populations often face higher exposures because of housing,

       ☆ BPA And Bisphenols: What To Watch For

                 ​Use glass, stainless steel, or ceramic for hot food and drinks
                 when possible.

                       ​Store leftovers in glass when you can.
                 ​Minimize handling of thermal paper receipts, especially right
                 after using hand sanitizer or lotion.
                 ​Choose fresh or frozen foods more often than heavily canned
                 foods when realistic.

           ​Phthalates are common in flexible plastics and can also hide inside
           fragrance in beauty and personal care products.
           ​They may show up in perfumes, fragranced lotions, air fresheners,
           vinyl products, plastic wrap, and some packaging.
                 ​This is one reason “fragrance” can be such a vague little
                 troublemaker! ​


           ☆ Simple Ways To Lower Phthalate Exposure
                 ​Choose   fragrance-free    or     clearly   labeled   low-fragrance
                 products more often, especially for daily-use items.
                       ​Reduce use of heavily fragranced sprays, plug-ins, and
                        synthetic air fresheners.
                 ​Avoid heating food in plastic wrap or soft plastic containers.

                 ​Simplify your routine a little! Fewer products can genuinely

           ​PFAS are called forever chemicals because they break down very
            slowly and can persist in the body and environment.
                 ​They are found in some non-stick cookware, stain-resistant
                  furniture,     waterproof      clothing,     grease-resistant     food
                  packaging, some cosmetics, and contaminated drinking water.
           ​They are associated in some studies with delayed conception,

            ☆ Simple Ways To Lower PFAS Exposure
                 ​Swap older scratched non-stick pans for stainless steel, cast
                  iron, or other lower-concern cookware when possible.
                 ​Cut   down      on    grease-resistant     fast-food   wrappers    and
                  microwave popcorn bags as routine habits.
                 ​Check local water information if you live near known
                  contamination sites, landfills, industrial areas, or military
                  bases.
                 ​Use a water filter certified for PFAS reduction if local
                  contamination is a concern.
                 ​Be cautious with heavily stain-resistant or water-repellent

           ​Air pollution is a real women’s-health issue, especially in pregnancy.

daily exposures matter. It is not always simple, but looking at the whole picture
can help women make sense of the uncertainty. ദ്ദി( • ᴗ • )

      ​Hot food? Try not to put it in plastic.

Superfoods & Cold-Pressed Juices
“Superfood” talk can sometimes feel like a high-speed chase through a wellness
trend-fest. And, to be honest, we've got better things to do! ( ￣＾￣) So, to not
waste your time, I’m skipping the hype so we can get straight to the good stuff
that actually works for you! And don’t worry（⌒▽⌒）— it’s not like you need a
magical berry flown in from a mountain at sunrise or anything weird like that. All
you need to understand is which foods actually give women meaningful nutritional
support, why they matter, and how they may fit into real life across your cycle,
reproductive years, and menopause.

This topic also gets confusing because some of the exact foods praised as
“superfoods” contain compounds called phytoestrogens. That word can sound scary,
especially when people hear phrases like “endocrine disruptor” and immediately
lose their marbles. But, as always, context matters so much! Many of these plant
compounds are found in normal foods, are consumed safely in regular diets, and may
offer antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, skin-supportive, and healthy-aging benefits
rather than harm.

202

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. Juices and
superfoods can support wellness, but they do not diagnose, cure, or replace
treatment for conditions like PCOS, endometriosis, infertility, UTIs, or menopause
symptoms. Think of them as supportive tools in a bigger care routine, not
miracle fixes. Use them to strengthen the foundation, not to carry the whole
house.


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Think of superfoods as your personal hype crew in edible form. (ง ˃ ³ ˂ )ɔ They’re
basically just standard ingredients packing a high concentration of support! They
tend to be especially rich in vitamins, minerals, fiber, antioxidants, and protective
plant compounds that can help the body handle inflammation, oxidative stress,
aging, and hormone-related changes a little more gracefully.


☆ What “Superfoods” Really Mean For Women
      ​Superfoods are foods especially rich in nutrients and protective compounds.
            ​They may help support energy, healthy aging, inflammation control,
             heart health, brain health, skin health, weight regulation, and
             hormone-related wellness.
            ​For women, certain superfoods may be especially useful during
             reproductive years, pregnancy, PMS, perimenopause, and menopause.
                  ​They are most helpful when eaten regularly as part of an overall
                   pattern, not treated like one-off miracle foods.

Okay, now it’s time to clear up a little science jumpscare! ദ്ദി(—ᴗ— ) People often
freak out over phytoestrogens, lumping them in with the infamous endocrine
disruptors. But here’s the tea: while they do interact with hormone pathways, they
aren’t the villains they’re made out to be. These compounds act as potent
antioxidants and anti-inflammatories! So the smarter question is not, “How do I
avoid all phytoestrogens?” It is, “What does the evidence actually say about them
in food?”

203

☆ What Phytoestrogens Actually Are
      ​Phytoestrogens are plant-derived polyphenols with some estrogen-like
      activity.
            ​Plants do not make human estrogen, but they do make compounds that
             can bind to estrogen receptors.
                    ​The four main classes are flavonoids, phenolic acids, lignans,
                    and stilbenes.
      ​These compounds are found in very normal foods and are basically impossible
      to fully avoid in everyday plant-based eating patterns.

      So, the most important nuance is that hormone-active               does   not
      automatically mean harmful.
            ​Phytoestrogens are not the same thing as estrogen.
            ​They may act more like weak, selective modulators rather than
             powerful hormone floods!
            ​Some appear to interact more strongly with ERβ, which is often
             discussed more favorably for skin and tissue support than ERα.
            ​Resveratrol and equol are recognized as compounds with promising
             skin-supportive and anti-aging potential.

             ☆ Why The Word “Endocrine Disruptor” Scares People Unnecessarily
             Here
                    ​Many people hear “endocrine disruptor” and assume it always
                    means toxic, dangerous, or hormone-damaging.
                          ​This is often a perspective problem rather than an
                           evidence-based conclusion!
                                ​Foods like berries, grapes, soy      foods, flax,
                                 legumes, cocoa, and leafy greens may contain
                                 phytoestrogens while also being widely celebrated
                                 as healthy foods.
                    ​The same food can be framed as a wellness food or a
                    hormone-active food depending on the lens being used.

204

                           ​That does not mean every hormone-active compound in
                           every   form    is   harmless. It means dietary     plant
                           compounds in normal foods deserve a much more nuanced
                           conversation.

☆ The Strongest Superfoods For Women: The Basic Eight
      ​There are eight especially useful foods for women.
      ​These are dark leafy greens, avocado, salmon, citrus fruits, pumpkin seeds,
      blueberries, ginger, and dark chocolate.
      ​Each one supports women’s health in a slightly different way.
      ​Together, they create a really practical foundation!


  1.​ Dark Leafy Greens
      ​Dark leafy greens like kale, spinach, and arugula are rich in folate.
            ​Folate supports cell growth and red blood cell production.
                    ​This makes leafy greens especially useful for prenatal health
                     and general women’s nutrition.
      ​Spinach and kale also contain helpful plant compounds such as flavonols and
      other polyphenols.
      ​So they support women through both core nutrition and plant-compound
      protection.


  2.​ Avocado
      ​Avocado supports satiety because it contains fiber and healthy fats.
            ​It also provides folate, potassium, vitamin E, and magnesium.
      ​Vitamin E and antioxidant-rich foods matter for skin integrity and healthy
      aging.


  3.​ Salmon
      ​Salmon is one of the strongest anti-inflammatory foods for women.
            ​It is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which may help lower inflammation
               and support heart health.
                    ​It also provides protein, B vitamins, and potassium.

205

      ​Anti-inflammatory foods matter because chronic inflammation contributes
      to skin aging, tissue stress, and broader disease risk.


  4.​ Citrus Fruits

Beyond the basics, many favorites like berries, soy, seeds, and leafy greens also

☆ Soy Foods: The Most Famous Phytoestrogen Example
      ​Soy is one of the best-known sources of isoflavones, a major subclass of
      phytoestrogens.
            ​Soy has been surrounded by repeated safety controversies, but the
             evidence does not support many common fears.
      ​Soy foods are not supported by the evidence as increasing overall cancer
      risk, meaningfully damaging thyroid function in most people, feminizing
      males, or drastically harming fertility in the ways people often claim.
            ​Instead, soy foods may offer positive contributions to health,
             especially in postmenopausal women.

☆ Resveratrol: The Superfood Compound People Accidentally Fear
      ​Resveratrol is a stilbene phytoestrogen found in red grape skins,
      blueberries, raspberries, cranberries, mulberries, peanuts, and cocoa
      powder.

207

            ​Yes, it is a phytoestrogen. So, yes, that means it is part of the
             broader hormone-active conversation.
                  ​But it is also a powerful antioxidant with anti-inflammatory and
                   skin-supportive effects! ^____^

      ☆ What Resveratrol May Do For Women
            ​Estrogen-deficient skin becomes more relevant with aging and
             menopause.
            ​After menopause, skin often becomes drier, more wrinkled, less
             elastic, and more vulnerable to collagen breakdown and oxidative
             stress.
                  ​Resveratrol may help by increasing antioxidant defenses,
                   supporting collagen and elastin-related pathways, reducing
                   inflammatory        signaling,    and       inhibiting   matrix
                   metalloproteinases, which are enzymes that break down
                   collagen and elastin.
            ​That is why it is framed as promising for anti-aging skin support,
             especially in women with lower estrogen levels.

☆ Equol: Another Important Compound For Women
      ​Equol is another major compound discussed in the review.
      ​It is related to soy isoflavone metabolism.
      ​It is described as especially promising for skin health in postmenopausal
      women.
      ​Equol may act like a selective estrogen receptor modulator, with particular
      interest around ERβ-related actions.
      ​It was associated with better collagen and elastin support, reduced
      inflammatory markers, protection against oxidative stress, and improved
      hydration, tone, and wrinkles.

      ☆ Why Equol Matters Specifically For Women
            ​Women move through major hormone shifts during puberty, the
             menstrual cycle, pregnancy, perimenopause, and menopause.

208

            ​In the menopause setting, where estrogen decline changes both the
             appearance and function of the skin, certain plant compounds with
             weak estrogen-like or receptor-modulating actions may be supportive
             rather than harmful.

Pre-Conception Checklist
A woman with a plan is truly a force to be reckoned with! And, as with all things, a
little bit of groundwork goes a long way. Whether you’re planning on pregnancy in
the near future or just keeping it in the “maybe someday” folder, focusing on
preconception care can make the process feel way less out of sorts. It is basically
the low-key preparation stage: making sure your body, mind, medications, and
daily habits are as supported as possible before pregnancy begins.

Think of it this way: prepping for a baby is not an all-or-nothing endeavor. It is
really just about layering in more support so your foundation feels steadier and
more secure. Tiny steps taken before conception can matter greatly because some
of the earliest stages of pregnancy happen before many women even realize they
are pregnant! (っ º - º ς)

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. If you are
actively trying to conceive, have chronic health conditions, take prescription
medications, or have a history of infertility, miscarriage, or mental health
concerns, it is especially worth checking in with a healthcare professional early.

218


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

A good preconception routine is less about doing everything at once and more about
covering the basics that actually protect you and a future pregnancy. Think of this
as your gentle, grown-woman checklist: preparation, not panic, and definitely not
pressure. Now, let’s get into it! (ദ്ദി˙ᗜ˙)

   1.​ Start With A Reproductive Life Plan
             ​A reproductive life plan means thinking about if you want children,
              when you might want them, and what steps would help you get there.
             ​This does not need to be rigid or overly formal.
             ​It simply helps you move from “I guess we will see?” to a more
              intentional mindset.
             ​It can also help you make smarter decisions now about contraception,
              timing, finances, health care, and lifestyle habits.

   2.​ See A Healthcare Professional Before Trying
             ​A preconception visit is one of the most useful things you can do.
             ​This is the time to review your medical history, current health
              conditions, past pregnancies, if applicable, and any medications or
              supplements you take.
             ​It is also the time to bring up things people often forget to ask about,
              like cycle irregularities, painful periods, thyroid issues, diabetes,
              high blood pressure, migraines, past eating issues, anxiety, depression,
              or family history concerns.
             ​The goal is to catch anything that could affect pregnancy early, not
              after you are already overwhelmed.

              ☆ What To Ask At A Preconception Appointment
                    ​Ask whether your current medications are safe to continue if
                     you become pregnant.
                    ​Ask whether you need any lab work, screening, or follow-up for
                     chronic conditions.

219

                ​Ask whether your cycle pattern suggests you are ovulating
                 regularly.
                ​Ask about your vaccine status to make sure you are all caught
                 up to date! (^-^)
                ​Ask what prenatal vitamin or folic acid routine makes sense for
                 you.
                ​Ask what health changes would be most helpful for your
                 specific body, not just for an imaginary textbook patient.

  3.​ Make Sure Your Vaccines Are Up To Date
          ​Being up to date on recommended vaccines before pregnancy can help
           protect both you and a future baby!
          ​The CDC specifically highlights MMR and the influenza vaccine as
           important parts of preconception care.
          ​This matters because some infections can be more dangerous during
           pregnancy, and some vaccines are ideally handled before conception
           rather than during it.
                ​If you are unsure what you have already had, your healthcare
                 professional can help you review your records.

  4.​ Take Folic Acid Before Pregnancy, Not After
          ​The CDC recommends that all women of reproductive age take 400
           micrograms of folic acid every day.
          ​This helps reduce the risk of major birth defects of the baby’s brain
           and spine, called neural tube defects.
          ​This step matters before pregnancy because the neural tube develops
           very early, often before a woman even realizes she is pregnant.

           ☆ Easy Folic Acid Tips
                ​Keep it by your toothbrush or skincare so you remember it
                 daily!
                ​Choose a simple routine you can actually stick to.
                ​Do not wait until a positive pregnancy test to start thinking
                 about it.

220

                ​If you already take a multivitamin or prenatal, check the label
                 so you know how much folic acid you are getting.

  5.​ Avoid Substances That Can Harm A Developing Baby
          ​Alcohol, tobacco, and illicit drugs can harm a developing baby at any
           stage, including very early pregnancy.
          ​That is why reducing or stopping them before conception is so
           strongly encouraged.
          ​This is not about shame. It is about timing and protection.
          ​If stopping feels difficult, that does not mean you failed. It means
           you deserve support, not silence. ( っ˶´ ˘ `)っ♡

           ☆ Harmful Substances To Pay Attention To
                ​Alcohol.
                ​Tobacco.
                ​Illicit drugs.
                ​Environmental toxins such as lead, mercury, BPA, phthalates,
                 PFAS, pesticides, and significant air pollution.

           ☆ Practical Ways To Reduce Exposure Before Pregnancy
                ​Avoid smoking and secondhand smoke.
                ​Be mindful of workplace or home exposures if you are around
                 chemicals, dust, fumes, or old paint.
                ​Limit unnecessary contact with known environmental toxins
                 when possible.
                ​Bring up home or job exposures at your medical visit, especially
                 if you work in health care, salons, factories, labs, agriculture,
                 construction, or other higher-exposure environments.

  6.​ Maintain A Healthy Weight In A Gentle, Sustainable Way
          ​Being at a healthy weight before pregnancy can lower the risk of
           complications such as gestational diabetes and preeclampsia.
          ​This does not mean crash dieting or trying to force your body into
           some impossible version of ideal! That is always a no-no!（ ￣へ￣）

221

           ​It means supporting your body with steady nutrition, movement, sleep,
           and medical guidance if needed.
           ​Pregnancy preparation should feel like care, not punishment.

      ☆ Weight-Supportive Habits That Are Actually Helpful
                 ​Eat regularly rather than swinging between restriction and
                   chaos.
                 ​Focus on balanced meals with protein, fiber, and nourishing
                   fats.
                 ​Choose movement that feels sustainable enough to repeat.
                 ​Ask your doctor what a healthy weight range means for you
                   specifically.
                 ​Avoid extreme diets right before trying to conceive.

  7.​ Manage Chronic Health Conditions Before Conception
           ​Conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, and depression can
           affect pregnancy if they are untreated or poorly controlled.
           ​Managing them ahead of time can lower the risk of complications for
           both you and the baby.
           ​This is one of the biggest reasons preconception care matters so
           much!
           ​Stable health going in often creates a much smoother road than trying
           to sort everything out mid-pregnancy.
                 ​This is not a sign that your body is “too complicated for
                   pregnancy” or anything absurd like that. It is just a matter of
                   taking thoughtful precaution. ( > ─ < )

           ☆ Conditions Worth Getting Under Better Control Beforehand
                 ​Diabetes.
                 ​High blood pressure.
                 ​Thyroid conditions.
                 ​Depression.
                 ​Anxiety.

222

                   ​Other ongoing medical conditions your doctor is already
                    tracking.

Mental health matters just as much as physical health! You do not need to
become the calmest woman alive before trying to conceive. That would be as
unrealistic as expecting yourself to float through life like a lavender-scented cloud
with perfect coping skills at all times. (ᵕ—ᴗ—) But untreated suffering should not
be brushed aside as just stress.
      ​Mental health is not extra credit. It is foundational.
      ​Untreated anxiety and depression can affect self-care, sleep, nutrition,
      stress levels, and day-to-day functioning.
      ​They are also associated with a higher risk of postpartum depression.
      ​So yes, being in a better place mentally before pregnancy really does matter!

      ☆ What Women Should Know About Mental Health And Pregnancy Planning
            ​If you are struggling emotionally, bring it up before pregnancy rather
             than hiding it.
            ​Many mental health medications are safe to continue during
             pregnancy!
            ​Some medications are not, which is exactly why talking with your
             healthcare provider early matters.
            ​Do not stop medication on your own just because you are thinking
             about pregnancy.
                   ​The safest plan is an informed plan!

   8.​ Mental Health Preparation Tips
            ​Tell your doctor if you have a history of anxiety, depression, panic
             attacks, OCD, trauma, or postpartum mental health issues.
            ​Ask whether your current treatment plan is pregnancy-safe.
            ​Build coping routines now, not only after conception.
            ​Prioritize sleep, nourishment, support, and emotional honesty.
            ​Let someone close to you know what support you may need.

☆ A Simple Preconception Checklist

223

      ​Think through your reproductive life plan.
      ​Book a preconception appointment.
      ​Review medical conditions and medications.
      ​Check vaccine status.
      ​Start 400 mcg folic acid daily.
      ​Reduce alcohol, tobacco, illicit drugs, and avoidable toxin exposure.
      ​Work toward a healthy weight in a supportive way.
      ​Get chronic conditions under better control.
      ​Take your mental health seriously before pregnancy, not as an afterthought.

☆ Gentle Reminder
      ​You do not need to do all of this in one crazy, hyper-organized weekend!
      ​You can build this checklist little by little. Bit by bit!
      ​One appointment, one supplement habit, one honest conversation, one
      healthier routine at a time is still real progress.
      ​Preparation does not need to be perfect to be meaningful. ♡



Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Preparing for pregnancy is really about creating steadiness before such a
life-changing   transition     begins.   The    goal   is   not     to   become    flawless,
ultra-disciplined, or oddly stress-free. It is to support your body, protect your
future baby where you can, and make sure your physical and mental health are both
part of the conversation. A gentle, informed start is more powerful than a
perfect one! ‹𝟹

Pelvic F loor Health
You know that one side character, the fan favorite who deserves the spotlight way
more than the main lead? That is the pelvic floor. It’s one of those parts of the
body so many women are never really taught about, even though it does the heavy
lifting for us behind the scenes every single day. It is a group of muscles that acts
like a supportive hammock at the base of the pelvis, helping hold up the bladder,
bowel, and, in women, the uterus.

When these muscles are working well, life tends to feel a lot more breezy and a lot
less complicated. When they are weak, overly tense, poorly coordinated, or
constantly strained, that is when leaks, pressure, discomfort, and other
frustrating symptoms can start popping up. So yes, pelvic floor health deserves
way more attention than it usually gets. (シ_ _ )シ

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. If you have
pelvic pain, pressure, prolapse symptoms, trouble emptying your bladder or bowels,
pain with sex, or worsening leakage, it is important to see a healthcare professional
or pelvic floor physical therapist rather than trying to push through it alone.

226


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

A healthy pelvic floor is not just about doing random Kegels and wishing on a
shooting star! It is really about support, coordination, strength, relaxation, and
protecting these muscles from too much repeated strain over time.

☆ Functions Of The Pelvic Floor
      ​The pelvic floor helps support the bladder, bowel, and uterus.
      ​It helps keep these organs in place so they do not shift downward more than
      they should.
      ​These muscles help open and close the sphincters, which is why they matter
      so much for bladder and bowel control.
      ​They also contribute to sexual health, including arousal, sensation, and
      orgasm.
            ​The pelvic floor works together with the diaphragm, abdominal
             muscles, and other core muscles to support posture, spinal stability,
             and pelvic balance.

Because your trusty pelvic floor handles everything from core stability to pressure
management, issues can show up in ways that seem completely unrelated and out of
the blue at first. It’s about so much more than just “not peeing yourself.” It is
about support, pressure management, stability, and comfort.

☆ Why Pelvic Floor Health Is Such A Big Deal For Women
      ​A well-functioning pelvic floor helps prevent urine leaks when you cough,
      laugh, sneeze, or move quickly.
      ​It helps support healthy bowel control too!
      ​It helps protect against excessive downward pressure that can contribute to
      prolapse, which is when organs start to shift or bulge downward.
      ​It supports core stability, which can affect balance, posture, and the way
      your body handles movement and lifting.
            ​It also matters for sexual well-being, which is something women are
             way too often expected to just magically figure out without good
             information. (ᵕ • ᴗ •)

227

So, how can you tell when your pelvic floor is waving a red flag?
      ​Urine leakage, especially when coughing, sneezing, jumping, or laughing.
      ​Trouble controlling gas or bowel movements.
      ​A feeling of heaviness, dragging, or pressure in the pelvis.
      ​A sense that something is bulging downward.
      ​Constipation linked to straining or pelvic coordination issues.
      ​Pain or discomfort with sex.
      ​Ongoing pelvic tension, especially if you feel like you are always clenching.

You know, a lot of women are under the assumption that these things are just
something they have to live with after childbirth or with aging. And I’m here to tell
you that, while they are common, you do not have to ignore them!

☆ Common Factors That Can Weaken Or Strain The Pelvic Floor
      ​Pregnancy, because carrying a growing baby places ongoing pressure on these
      muscles.
      ​Vaginal childbirth, because delivery can stretch and weaken the pelvic floor.
      ​Aging, because pelvic floor muscles can lose strength and flexibility over
      time like other muscles do.
      ​Chronic constipation and repeated straining.
      ​Heavy lifting done with poor pressure management.
      ​A persistent cough that keeps bearing down on the pelvic floor.
      ​Obesity, because extra body weight creates ongoing pressure on the pelvic
      floor.

This is helpful to know because it reminds you that pelvic floor changes are not
random. There are usually real mechanical reasons behind them. And, since it’s a
physical system, it responds to physical solutions. (ง ˃ ᗜ ˂)ว .ˊˎ-

   1.​ Kegel Exercises Can Help, But Only If You Are Doing Them Correctly
               ​Kegels are one of the best-known ways to support pelvic floor
               strength.
               ​They involve squeezing and lifting the pelvic floor muscles, then
               letting them relax fully.

228

              ​A simple image is to imagine you are trying to stop the flow of
               urine and hold back gas at the same time.
      ​The squeeze should feel internal and supportive, not like you are
      gripping your thighs, clenching your butt, or bracing your whole body.
      ( ˃̩﹏˂̩
         ̩̥ ̩̥ ͒)

      ☆ Tips For Doing Kegels The Right Way
              ​Start gently rather than squeezing as hard as humanly possible.
              ​Lift and squeeze the pelvic floor, then fully relax.
              ​Breathe normally while you do them.
              ​Keep your stomach, butt, and thighs as relaxed as possible.
              ​Focus on quality over speed.
              ​Do not turn every Kegel into a full-body stress event.
                    ​Feel free to refer to the image below, heavily inspired by
                     Prevail eNurse Team, n.d. :-)

229

           ☆ What To Avoid With Kegels
                    ​Do not practice by repeatedly stopping your urine flow during
                    actual bathroom trips.
                    ​Do not hold your breath.
                    ​Do not bear down or push downward instead of lifting upward.
                    ​Do not assume more squeezing is always better.
                    ​Do not keep doing them if they increase pain or tension without
                    getting professional guidance.


  2.​ Relaxation Is Part Of Pelvic Floor Health Too
          ​A healthy pelvic floor is not only strong. It also needs to relax.
          ​These muscles should soften and lengthen when appropriate,
           especially during inhalation, bowel movements, and general pressure
           release.
          ​If a woman is constantly clenching, bracing, or living in stress mode,
           the pelvic floor may stay too tense.
          ​That      tension   can   contribute   to   discomfort,   pain,   and   poor
           coordination.


  3.​ Diaphragmatic Breathing Helps More Than People Realize
          ​When you inhale, the diaphragm moves down and the pelvic floor
           naturally relaxes and lengthens.
          ​When you exhale, the diaphragm rises and the pelvic floor naturally
           lifts.
          ​This coordination is part of healthy core function.
          ​If breathing is shallow, tense, or constantly chest-driven, that natural
           rhythm can get disrupted.

           ☆ Easy Diaphragmatic Breathing Cues
                    ​Breathe in slowly and let your ribs and belly expand.
                    ​Imagine the pelvic floor gently softening on the inhale.
                    ​Exhale and feel a light lift through the lower core and pelvic
                    floor.
                    ​Keep the jaw, shoulders, and glutes relaxed.

230



  4.​ Avoid Straining Whenever Possible
          ​Repeated straining is one of the biggest things that can wear down
           the pelvic floor over time.
          ​This includes straining during constipation, forcing urine out quickly,
           or constantly pushing through heavy pressure.
                 ​The more often you bear down hard, the more stress these
                  muscles and supportive tissues have to absorb.
          ​Preventing that repeated strain is one of the most practical forms of
           pelvic floor care.

           ☆ Ways To Reduce Straining In Daily Life
                 ​Eat enough fiber to support regular bowel movements.
                 ​Stay hydrated.
                 ​Give yourself enough time in the bathroom instead of rushing.
                 ​Let your bladder empty naturally rather than forcing it.
                 ​Treat chronic constipation rather than acting like it’s normal.
                 ​Get support for a chronic cough if one is present.


  5.​ Avoid Power Peeing
          ​Power peeing means straining to empty your bladder fast instead of
           letting it flow naturally.
          ​It may feel efficient in the moment, but it can train poor pressure
           habits and add unnecessary pelvic floor stress.
          ​A calmer, more relaxed bladder-emptying pattern is better for
           long-term function.


  6.​ Maintain A Healthy Weight If Possible
          ​Excess body weight places ongoing pressure on the pelvic floor.
          ​Over time, that constant extra load can make it harder for the
           muscles and connective tissues to keep everything supported well.
          ​Now, weight management is not about perfection here. It is about
           reducing mechanical stress where you reasonably can! ^___^ Even
           modest changes can help reduce pressure.

231



   7.​ Posture And Body Mechanics Matter Too
            ​Poor pressure management during lifting, standing, or sitting can
             increase stress on the pelvic floor.
            ​The pelvic floor works as part of a bigger team, so posture and core
             coordination affect it.
            ​Slumped, rigid, or poorly supported movement patterns can make
             symptoms worse over time.
            ​Gentle awareness helps a lot here.

             ☆ Lifting Tips That Protect The Pelvic Floor
                  ​Engage your core gently before lifting.
                  ​Exhale through effort rather than holding your breath.
                  ​Lift with your legs instead of yanking with your back and belly
                   pressure.
                  ​Avoid sudden, forceful bearing down.
                  ​Get help with very heavy loads when you can.

Now for the main event: pregnancy and postpartum. These stages put a unique kind
of demand on your pelvic floor:
      ​Pregnancy puts real physical demands on the pelvic floor because of
      increasing weight and pressure.
      ​Childbirth, especially vaginal delivery, can stretch and weaken these muscles
      further.
            ​That does not mean damage is guaranteed, but it does mean support
             and recovery matter.
      ​Postpartum women are often told to just wait things out, but pelvic floor
      care can be incredibly helpful during recovery.

      ☆ Gentle Pelvic Floor Support During Pregnancy And Postpartum
            ​Use breathing and pressure management instead of constant bracing.
            ​Avoid chronic constipation.
            ​Be mindful with lifting, especially while healing.

232

             ​Talk to your provider if you notice heaviness, leaking, pain, or
             pressure.
             ​Consider pelvic floor physical therapy if symptoms are lingering.

And, as mentioned earlier, aging does not mean you have to give up on pelvic floor
function.
      ​Like other muscles, the pelvic floor can lose strength and flexibility with
      age.
      ​That may increase the likelihood of symptoms like leaking, prolapse, or pelvic
      heaviness.
             ​But this is not a lost-cause situation.
      ​Supportive exercise, breathing, healthy bowel habits, and treatment, when
      needed, can still make a real difference.

We can’t ignore the connection to intimacy, either! Your pelvic floor is a central
player in sexual health and overall comfort.
      ​The pelvic floor contributes to arousal, sensation, and orgasm.
      ​If these muscles are weak, overly tight, painful, or poorly coordinated,
      sexual comfort and function can be affected.
             ​Pelvic health information must include pleasure and comfort, not just
             leakage prevention.

☆ When To Get Extra Help
      ​If symptoms are persistent.
      ​If you feel pressure or bulging.
      ​If leakage is getting worse.
      ​If sex is painful.
      ​If you cannot seem to identify the right muscles.
      ​If Kegels make things feel tighter, more painful, or more uncomfortable.

A pelvic floor physical therapist can be such a game-changer here! Sometimes the
issue is weakness, sometimes it is tension, and sometimes it is coordination.
Knowing which one you are dealing with matters a lot.

☆ A Gentle Daily Pelvic Floor Routine

233

      ​Check your posture a few times during the day.
      ​Practice diaphragmatic breathing for a few minutes.
      ​Avoid constipation and rushing in the bathroom.
      ​Use Kegels thoughtfully, not frantically.
      ​Exhale during effort when lifting or standing from a heavy task.
      ​Notice whether you are clenching when stressed and consciously let go.


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Pelvic floor health matters because these muscles support so many basic parts of
daily life, from bladder control to bowel function to posture to sexual well-being! A
strong, coordinated pelvic floor can make your body feel more supported and more
comfortable, while an overstrained one can create symptoms that are easy to
dismiss but hard to live with. The good news is that awareness, good habits, and
the right support can go a long way! Your pelvic floor is not random background
tissue. It is part of your foundation, and it deserves quality care. (⸝⸝⸝>﹏<⸝⸝⸝) ♡⸝⸝
