             Pregnancy Wellness
      Chapter 5: Nourishing Yourself While Pregnant

236




Pregnancy Nutrition
If you hopped on Google right now and searched for common pregnancy questions,
one of the first results would likely be, “What do I eat while pregnant?” And I
mean, hey, it makes sense! ┐(´∀｀)┌


Pregnancy nutrition has a tendency to feel oddly overwhelming because suddenly
every morsel of food seems to come with a rule, a warning, or a dramatic opinion
from somebody on the web. But the heart of it is actually much simpler: your body
is doing a miraculous amount of work, and it needs steady nourishment, enough
variety, and a little extra intention.


So, by all means, forget about trying to “eat like a saint.” There’s no need! The main
objective is helping your body feel supported while giving your baby the building
blocks they need for growth, development, and safety. A few key nutrients matter
especially, and a few food-safety habits matter a lot too!

237

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. If you have
severe nausea, vomiting, food aversions, anemia, gestational diabetes, high blood
pressure, a multiple pregnancy, or dietary restrictions that make eating hard, it is
important to talk with your healthcare provider or a registered dietitian for
personalized support.


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

No need to fret! ( ⌒ _ ⌒ ) A healthy pregnancy diet is not about chasing
perfection or eating for two in some dramatic, stressful way. It’s simply building
meals around the nutrients that matter most, staying hydrated, and avoiding a few
foods that carry higher safety risks. That’s all there is to it! You do not need a
Pinterest-perfect meal plan. You need a pattern that actually nourishes you.


☆ The Big-Picture Goal
      ​Focus on nutrient-dense foods rather than just eating more food.
      ​Aim for meals that include protein, fiber-rich carbohydrates, healthy fats,
       vitamins, and minerals from a variety of foods.
      ​Think in terms of support, not restriction.
             ​Consistency matters more than having a perfect day of eating!

Pregnancy nutrition works best when it feels doable. So, at the end of the day,
your task is a piece of cake: just help your body feel steady, fueled, and genuinely
cared for in real life!

☆ Folic Acid And Folate: One Of The Most Important Early Nutrients
      ​Folic acid and folate are crucial for helping prevent neural tube defects.
      ​This matters especially early in pregnancy, often before many women even
       know they are pregnant.
      ​Foods that provide folate include dark green leafy vegetables like spinach
       and broccoli, citrus fruits like oranges, beans, peas, and fortified cereals.

☆ Iron: For Extra Blood Volume And Anemia Prevention

238

      ​Iron is needed to help make the extra blood your body needs during
      pregnancy.
      ​It also helps reduce the risk of anemia, which can leave you feeling
      exhausted, weak, or short of breath.
      ​Good food sources include lean red meat, poultry, fish, dried beans, peas,
      iron-fortified cereals, and spinach.
            ​Fun fact: Pairing iron-rich foods with vitamin C sources can improve
               absorption!

      ☆ Easy Iron Pairings That Make The Iron You Are Already Eating More
      Useful To Your Body
            ​Spinach & oranges.
            ​Beans & tomatoes.
            ​Iron-fortified cereal & berries.
            ​Lean meat & bell peppers.
            ​Lentils & citrus.

               That pairing trick is such a good one because it does not require a
               full-blown diet makeover. It simply helps your body get more use out
               of the iron you are already eating.

☆ Calcium And Vitamin D: For Bones, Teeth, Muscles, And More
      ​Calcium and vitamin D work together to help build your baby’s bones and
      teeth.
      ​They also support the baby’s heart, nerves, and muscles.
      ​For the mother, they help maintain bone density.
      ​Adequate intake is also linked with helping reduce the risk of preeclampsia,
      which is a pregnancy complication involving high blood pressure and protein
      in the urine.

      ☆ Calcium-Rich Foods
            ​Milk.
            ​Yogurt.
            ​Cheese.

239

            ​Calcium-fortified orange juice.
            ​Dark green leafy vegetables like kale and spinach.

      ☆ Vitamin D-Rich Foods
            ​Fortified milk.
            ​Fatty fish like salmon.
            ​Eggs.

      You see, calcium gets a lot of the attention, but vitamin D helps the body
      use it properly. A very “please don’t forget my bestie” nutrient pair!

☆ Protein: A Major Building Block During Pregnancy
      ​Protein supports the growth of fetal tissue.
      ​It also supports the growth of breast tissue and uterine tissue.
      ​Good protein sources include lean meat, poultry, seafood, eggs, beans, peas,
      nuts, seeds, and soy products like tofu.
            ​Protein can also help meals feel more steady and satisfying, which is
             extra helpful when pregnancy appetite gets unpredictable.

      ☆ Simple Ways To Add More Protein Without Making Meals Complicated
            ​Add eggs to breakfast.
            ​Include beans or lentils in soups, bowls, or salads.
            ​Build snacks around yogurt, nuts, or cheese.
            ​Add tofu or lean meat to grain bowls.
                     ​Keep protein in every main meal when you can!

                     Protein is just one of those nutrients that subtly makes
                     everything work better. She’s not always glamorous, but she is
                     doing a lot!

☆ Omega-3 Fatty Acids: Especially Important For Baby’s Brain And Eyes
      ​Omega-3 fatty acids are important for brain and eye development.
      ​Low-mercury fish like salmon, sardines, and herring are especially helpful
      food sources.
      ​Other sources include walnuts, flaxseed, and canola oil.

240

      If fish feels hard to eat during pregnancy because of nausea or aversions,
      that’s okay! It just means you may need other strategies or a conversation
      with your provider. ദ്ദി ´⌣` )

☆ Iodine: Small Nutrient, Very Big Job
      ​Iodine is critical for the baby’s brain development.
      ​Good sources include iodized table salt, dairy products, seafood, and eggs.
            ​This nutrient tends to get overlooked because folate and iron usually
             get more attention, so consider this iodine’s little moment in the light.
             ( ∴• v •∴ )

☆ Potassium: Underrated But Helpful
      ​Potassium supports fluid and electrolyte balance.
      ​It may help with swelling and leg cramps.
      ​It is also important for maintaining healthy blood pressure.
      ​Good sources include bananas, sweet potatoes, avocados, spinach, beans,
      lentils, and dairy products.

      Pregnancy can make your body feel extra puffy and crampy at times, so
      potassium-rich foods can be a really practical part of daily support.

☆ Vitamin K: Important For Clotting And Healing
      ​Vitamin K is important for proper blood clotting.
      ​This matters for wound healing and can help support the body’s ability to
      prevent excessive bleeding during labor and delivery.
      ​Good food sources include leafy greens like kale, spinach, and collard
      greens, as well as broccoli, Brussels sprouts, and cabbage.
      ​It is one of those nutrients that does important behind-the-scenes work.

☆ Hydration Matters More Than People Think
      ​Water helps support circulation, digestion, and overall pregnancy comfort.
      ​A simple goal is around 8 glasses of water throughout the day.
      ​Staying hydrated can also help with constipation, headaches, and that
      washed-out, low-energy feeling.

241

            ​This one is commonly looked over, but water truly is a boring
             afterthought until you are dehydrated, and then suddenly she is the
             star of the show! (。￣。)

      ☆ Gentle Hydration Tips
            ​Sip throughout the day instead of waiting until you feel awful.
            ​Keep water near you.
            ​Pair fluids with meals and snacks.
            ​Use fruit or ice if plain water feels unappealing.
            ​Ask for help if nausea is making hydration really hard.

Now that we’ve covered all the good stuff your body needs, let’s chat about a few
things you’ll want to be a bit more cautious with for a while!

☆ Caffeine: Not Forbidden, But Limited
      ​Caffeine should be limited to less than 200 milligrams per day.
            ​That is about 1 to 2 cups of coffee, depending on the strength and
             serving size.
      ​So, please, do not lose it over one measly cup! Remember: moderation is key.

☆ Alcohol: Avoid Completely
      ​No amount of alcohol is considered safe during pregnancy.
      ​This is one of the clearest nutrition rules in pregnancy guidance!
      ​If avoiding alcohol feels emotionally hard or socially complicated, that does
      not make you a bad person whatsoever. It just means support may help.
            ​Safety here matters more than trying to seem low-maintenance
             about it.

☆ High-Mercury Fish To Avoid
      ​Avoid shark, swordfish, king mackerel, and tilefish.
      ​Limit white albacore tuna to 6 ounces per week.

      So, no, this is not about avoiding fish altogether. It is about choosing
      lower-mercury options more thoughtfully.

242

☆ Foods To Avoid Because Of Foodborne Illness Risk
      ​Unpasteurized milk.
      ​Unpasteurized juices.
      ​Soft cheeses made from unpasteurized milk, including cheeses like Brie,
      feta, and blue cheese.
      ​Raw or undercooked meat.
      ​Raw or undercooked poultry.
      ​Raw or undercooked seafood.
      ​Raw or undercooked eggs.
      ​Foods made with raw eggs, like raw cookie dough.
      ​Raw sprouts of any kind.

      Pregnancy lowers the margin for error with food safety a bit, which is why
      these rules matter. It is less about fear and more about reducing avoidable
      risk.

☆ Why Raw Sprouts Are One Of Those Sneaky Pregnancy No’s
      ​The warm, humid conditions used to grow sprouts are also ideal for harmful
      bacteria.
              ​That includes bacteria like Salmonella, E. coli, and Listeria.
      ​Because of that, raw sprouts are considered riskier during pregnancy.
      ​This one surprises people a lot, but it is a real food-safety issue!

☆ Deli Meats Need One Extra Step
      ​Deli meats should be heated until steaming hot before eating.
      ​This is to help kill potential bacteria, especially Listeria.
      ​It is a small habit, but it matters.
              ​Pregnancy really is an era of “annoying but useful precautions,” and
              this is one of them.

☆ A Simple Way To Build A Pregnancy-Supportive Plate
      ​Include a protein source.
      ​Add a vegetable or fruit.
      ​Include a fiber-rich carbohydrate.

243

      ​Add calcium-rich or iron-rich foods across the day.
      ​Use hydration as part of the meal pattern, not an afterthought.
            ​Take a look at the plate below from Raising Children Network,
             “Healthy Eating for Pregnancy.” It’s a simple visual guide for how
             those food groups can fit together! Don’t get caught up in the stress
             of exact measurements; just aiming to get a little bit of each group
             onto your plate is a win. ♡




That kind of structure helps make pregnancy nutrition feel less abstract. Please
keep in mind that you do not need to memorize a giant chart every time you eat!
You just need a few consistent anchors.

☆ If Eating Feels Difficult, Focus On Gentle Wins
      ​Small meals still count.
      ​Bland food still counts.
      ​Repeating safe foods is okay for a while.
      ​A decent meal is still a good meal.

244

             ​Nutrition during pregnancy should support you, not become another
              thing you use to scare yourself.

Some phases of pregnancy are very much survival mode. That is valid. If nausea,
cravings, aversions, exhaustion, or food sensitivity are running rampant for a while,
take the pressure down where you can. Keep choosing the next gentle step: a sip,
a snack, a safe food, a small meal, or a provider check-in when you need one.


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

A healthy pregnancy diet doesn’t have to look fancy to be deeply supportive. When
you focus on key nutrients, stay hydrated, choose safer food options, and build
meals with a little more intention, you are giving both your body and your baby
something really meaningful! Nourishment during pregnancy is not about being
picture-perfect. It is about being cared for, supported, and steady, one meal at a
time.

How to Deal With Pregnancy Cravings
Pregnancy cravings are like a security guard who will not let you pass until you
answer a riddle that can only be solved by a very specific brand of spicy chips.
They’re… erratic, to say the least. (⸝⸝⸝-﹏-⸝⸝⸝) One day something sounds
delectable, and the next day the smell alone makes you want to flee the scene
immediately. If that flip-flop has ever made you feel confused, dramatic, guilty, or
like your body is suddenly operating with a secret menu, please know: you are
absolutely not alone.

Cravings are common, but they can still bring up very real questions about
nutrition, weight gain, and whether your body is trying to tell you something. The
good news is that most cravings are not a cause for concern. You do not need to
control every bite or turn every snack into a huge deal! Understanding what is
happening, then responding with a little more calm, balance, and support, is all that
is necessary.

247

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. If cravings
become extreme, involve non-food items, or come with concerns about nutrition,
iron, weight gain, or hydration, it is important to check in with your healthcare
provider.


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

“If life were a movie, I’d be sending someone out into a rainstorm at midnight just
to find a very specific brand of crunchy peanut butter.” ( ` ᴖ ´ )

Ah yes. We have all seen those jokes, and while they make great Reddit fodder,
there is actually real biology behind the cravings. They are not just you being “too
emotional” or “dramatic.” Your senses, hormones, appetite signals, and day-to-day
needs really can shift during pregnancy.

☆ What Causes Pregnancy Cravings
      ​Hormonal changes, including shifts in hCG, progesterone, and estrogen, can
      heighten smell and taste sensitivity.
            ​That increased sensitivity can make some foods sound intensely
             appealing and others suddenly unbearable. （・．・；）
                   ​Taste and smell changes can also contribute to food aversions,
                    which may sometimes play a protective role by making certain
                    foods less appealing.
      ​Some researchers also explore whether cravings can occasionally reflect
      nutrient needs, but this is not a simple one-to-one rule.

So yes, sometimes a craving is, well, just a craving. Sometimes it may loosely line up
with a need. Usually, it is best to think of cravings as information, not instructions.

☆ When Cravings Usually Start And How Long They Last
      ​Cravings can begin as early as the first trimester.
      ​For many women, they ease up after the first trimester.
      ​For others, they continue on and off throughout pregnancy.

248

            ​There is a wide range of normal here, so timing can vary a lot from
             person to person.

      ☆ Cravings And Aversions Often Come Together
            ​Pregnancy does not just increase cravings. It can also create strong
             food aversions.
            ​A food you used to love may suddenly feel impossible to tolerate.
            ​Strong smells, textures, or flavors may hit differently during
             pregnancy.
            ​In some cases, aversions may help steer women away from foods that
             feel unsafe, spoiled, or harder to tolerate.

      This is why forcing yourself to eat something just because it is “healthy” can
      backfire if it is making you feel crummy or straight up nauseated.
      Sometimes the better move is finding a gentler alternative that still
      supports you.

☆ Most Cravings Are Harmless
      ​Common cravings like chocolate, chips, fruit, salty foods, sour foods, or
      spicy foods are usually not dangerous by themselves.
      ​The bigger issue is the overall pattern of eating, not one random craving.
      ​A craving becomes more important when it is constant, extreme, or pushing
      out more nourishing foods too often.
      ​The key is always balance.

      In other words, craving a brownie does not mean you are doing pregnancy
      wrong. It just means you are human and pregnant, which is already more
      than enough excitement for one body! :,) ♡

☆ Pica Is Different And Needs Attention
      ​Pica means craving or eating non-food or non-nutritive substances, such as
      dirt, clay, soap, paper, or ice.
            ​Pica is less common than typical food cravings, but it is still
             important.
      ​It may sometimes be linked with deficiencies such as low iron or low calcium.

249

      ​It can also create health risks depending on what is being eaten.

      If cravings move into non-food territory, that is not something to quietly
      shrug off. It is a real reason to contact your healthcare provider.

      ☆ What Pica Can Signal
            ​Possible nutritional deficiencies, especially iron deficiency, are one
               concern.
            ​Some substances can expose you to bacteria, toxins, intestinal
               problems, or injury.
            ​Even if it feels embarrassing to mention, it is medically important and
               worth bringing up.
            ​Early support can help protect both you and your baby.

Now, you have probably heard the old “eating for two” cliché a thousand times, but
when it comes to extra calories, the reality is actually a lot less exaggerated than
people typically think!
      ​You do not need to “eat for two” in the literal sense. (〃´▽`〃)
            ​During pregnancy, extra calorie needs are usually smaller than people
               anticipate: many women need no extra calories in the first trimester,
               about 340 extra calories per day in the second trimester, and about
               450 extra calories per day in the third trimester.
      ​That usually looks more like one additional snack than a whole extra day of
      meals!
            ​Quality matters just as much as quantity.

      ☆ Healthy Weight Gain Recommendations Depend On Pre-Pregnancy BMI
            ​Underweight, with a BMI under 18.5: about 28 to 40 pounds.
            ​Normal weight, with a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9: about 25 to 35 pounds.
            ​Overweight, with a BMI of 25 to 29.9: about 15 to 25 pounds.
            ​Obese, with a BMI of 30 or greater: about 11 to 20 pounds.
                    ​Carrying multiples, like twins or triplets, usually increases these
                     ranges.

250

      Weight gain is merely one clinical tool used to support pregnancy health, and
      it should be interpreted with your body, your history, your symptoms, and
      your provider’s guidance in mind.

☆ Why Balancing Cravings Matters
      ​Excessive weight gain and poor nutrition can raise the risk of gestational
      diabetes.
      ​They can also increase the likelihood of cesarean             birth, delivery
      complications, and postpartum weight retention.
      ​For the baby, concerns can include larger-than-average size, blood sugar
      issues, and longer-term obesity risk.
      ​That does not mean every craving causes harm. It means patterns matter
      over time.

      All-or-nothing thinking is usually counterproductive here, like it usually is in
      most life situations. Constant restriction is a headache. But on the other
      hand, constant “anything goes” can also stop feeling good pretty fast.
      ヽ(；▽；)ノ

The middle ground is the sweet spot!

☆ The Best Mindset: Cravings Are Signals, Not Commands
      ​Cravings are normal and natural.
      ​Sometimes they may reflect changing senses more than an actual deficiency.
      ​Sometimes they may loosely overlap with what your body needs, but not
      always.
      ​It helps to pause and ask what would satisfy you while still supporting your
      body.

      ☆ Tips For Handling Cravings Without Feeling Deprived
              ​Try to pair the craving with something more nourishing instead of
              fighting it aggressively.
              ​If you want something sweet, see whether fruit, yogurt, or fruit plus
              protein could help first.

251

            ​If you still want the actual craving afterward, have some and move on
             without spiraling.
            ​Planning satisfying snacks ahead of time makes it much easier not to
             get ambushed by hunger.

             ☆ Better Snack Ideas When Cravings Hit
                   ​Yogurt or cottage cheese for protein and calcium.
                   ​Fruit with nuts or nut butter for fiber, healthy fats, and more
                   staying power.
                   ​Whole grain toast with something protein-rich.
                   ​Lean meats, eggs, or fish when savory cravings show up.
                   ​Vegetables with a dip or grain bowl when you want something
                   crunchy or filling.

A lot of intense craving “emergencies” are at least partly “I accidentally waited too
long to eat” situations. ( ；´‸｀) Smaller, more frequent meals can help.
      ​Eating every few hours may be easier than trying to power through big gaps
      between meals.
            ​Smaller meals can help with nausea, energy dips, and that strange
             pregnancy combo of being hungry and queasy at the same time.
                   ​More frequent eating may also make cravings feel less urgent.
      ​Long stretches without food can make it much harder to respond calmly.

☆ Hydration Matters More Than People Realize
      ​Aim for around 8 to 12 cups of water per day.
      ​Dehydration can make fatigue, headaches, dizziness, and feeling-off
      sensations worse.
      ​Sometimes what feels like a food craving is really your body needing fluid.
      ​Keeping water nearby throughout the day makes this much easier.

Now, it is worth noting that your pregnancy body may have different rules than
your pre-pregnancy body. A pain in the you-know-what, yes. Personal betrayal,
maybe. (¬_¬”) But still worth working with.
      ​Many pregnant women deal with GERD, which is acid reflux.

252

      ​Spicy or irritating foods can make that worse for some people.
      ​If a craving keeps leading to burning, discomfort, or chest pressure, it may
      help to choose a gentler version.
      ​This is less about “good” or “bad” food and more about noticing what your
      body tolerates right now.

☆ Prenatal Vitamins Still Matter
      ​Prenatal vitamins help cover nutritional gaps.
      ​They are especially important for nutrients like folic acid.
      ​Vitamins do not replace food, but they do help support the baby when
      appetite, nausea, or inconsistent eating make things harder.
      ​They are part of the safety net, not the whole plan.

Okay, now for the cherry on top! There might also be a brain-reward piece
happening since research shows pregnancy cravings can actually light up specific
reward pathways in your head. ( ￣□￣；）


This possible physiology is why certain foods feel so emotionally charged and
intense, so please know it’s not a lack of willpower. It may just be a very pregnant
brain doing its thing! While you might wonder if craving ice cream or fruit is your
body’s way of signaling a nutrient deficiency like calcium or vitamins, these links
are interesting but not definitive. A craving on its own isn’t a diagnosis, but
understanding the science can help you stop blaming yourself for those sudden,
“must-have-it-now” moments! :-)


☆ When To Call Your Healthcare Provider
      ​If cravings involve non-food substances.
      ​If you are unable to keep nourishing foods down.
      ​If weight gain feels very fast, very low, or concerning.
      ​If food aversions are so strong that you are struggling to eat enough.
      ​If you are worried about iron, calcium, hydration, or overall nutrition.

      Bringing it up is not overreacting. That is literally what they are there for!

253

☆ A Gentle Strategy That Usually Works Best
   1.​ Notice the craving.
   2.​ Ask whether you are hungry, thirsty, nauseated, tired, or overstimulated.
   3.​ Choose a nourishing option first when possible.
   4.​ Let yourself have the craving in moderation when that feels right.
   5.​ Keep the overall week balanced instead of obsessing over one little moment.


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Pregnancy cravings can be weird, strong, emotional, and honestly kind of
inconvenient, but they are also very normal. You do not need to fear them, obey
them blindly, or judge yourself for having them. The best approach is to stay
curious, stay nourished, and stay flexible. Your body is doing a lot right now, and it
deserves a truckload of support, not a courtroom trial over every snack. ⋆˙⟡

Navigating Morning Sickness
The usual morning spent hunched over a toilet and hurling while the rest of the
world drinks coffee… fun stuff, huh? Morning sickness is one of those pregnancy
symptoms people mention so casually, but when you are the one actually living it, it
can feel exhausting, puzzling, and, to be perfectly honest, kind of humbling!
(っ╥﹏╥ς) It can show up as nausea, retching, vomiting, food aversions, or all of
the above, and despite the name, it absolutely does not clock out after breakfast.

The reassuring part is that morning sickness is extremely common, especially in
early pregnancy. In many cases, it may even reflect a protective response during a
sensitive stage of development rather than a sign that something is “wrong.” Still,
common does not mean easy. A lot of the “common” parts of pregnancy can still
feel like an uphill battle and a half. And, through it all, you deserve support,
strategy, and a little less “just sit through it with a smile” energy.

As always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. Mild to
moderate nausea can be a normal part of pregnancy, but severe vomiting,
dehydration, inability to keep food or fluids down, weight loss, dizziness, or signs
of weakness deserve medical attention.

256


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Morning sickness is often called morning sickness, but that name is a teensy bit
misleading! For many women, symptoms can show up at any point during the day and
can make the whole first trimester feel very different from what they expected.


☆ What Morning Sickness Actually Is
      ​Morning sickness refers to nausea and vomiting during pregnancy.
      ​Medically, it is often called NVP, which stands for nausea and vomiting in
      pregnancy.
      ​It may also be called pregnancy sickness or emesis gravidarum.
      ​Common symptoms include nausea, retching, vomiting, and food aversions.
      ​It usually shows up during the first trimester.

If you are dealing with this, you are very much not alone. Morning sickness is one
of the most common early-pregnancy experiences in the world.
      ​About two-thirds of pregnant women experience nausea and vomiting in
      pregnancy.
      ​Across many estimates, the average frequency is around 68%.
      ​Rates can range widely, from mild nausea in some women to more persistent
      vomiting in others.

Now, please, take a breath. (っ´        `)っ This is not the end-all-be-all. For many
women, symptoms really do ease with time, even if it feels like your stomach is
calling all the shots in the moment.
      ​Symptoms often begin around week 4 of pregnancy.
             ​They usually rise fairly quickly after that.
      ​Symptoms tend to peak around weeks 9 to 14.
             ​They then gradually decline for many women.
      ​By around week 20, most women feel significant improvement.

As mentioned before, morning sickness does not only happen in the morning. If
your “morning” sickness hits at 2 p.m., after dinner, or whenever your body feels
like causing a scene, that still counts!

257

      ​Symptoms can happen throughout the waking hours of the day.
      ​Nausea often appears during daytime hours.
      ​Symptoms are usually less common during sleep.
      ​Some women feel their worst first thing in the morning, but many do not!

☆ Why Researchers Think It May Happen
      ​One fascinating scientific theory is this: morning sickness may help protect
      the developing embryo.
      ​Nausea and vomiting may encourage the body to avoid or expel foods that
      could contain toxins, pathogens, or compounds that interfere with
      development.
      ​These may include teratogens, which are chemicals that can cause birth
      defects.
      ​They may also include abortifacients, which are substances that may
      increase miscarriage risk.

While it may feel like a total ambush, pregnancy nausea is not just some random
plot twist appearing out of nowhere to sabotage your lunch plans. >___< It often
peaks right when the embryo is especially sensitive.
      ​The most sensitive developmental window is roughly weeks 6 to 12 of
      pregnancy.
      ​During this time, organ systems are forming.
      ​Cell division and differentiation are happening rapidly.
      ​That means the embryo is especially vulnerable to chemical disruption during
      this stretch.

☆ Foods That Commonly Trigger Aversions
      ​Pregnant women often develop aversions to foods that historically may have
      been more likely to carry toxins or pathogens.
      ​Common aversions include meat, fish, poultry, and eggs.
      ​Alcoholic beverages are also commonly avoided.
      ​Caffeinated drinks like coffee and tea often become less appealing.
      ​Strong-tasting vegetables and foods with strong odors can also become
      harder to tolerate.

258

      ​The strongest aversions are often toward animal products.

It turns out your body is operating on a much lower tolerance threshold than usual
right now. While it feels like you are just being “picky,” food disgust during
pregnancy can have much deeper biological roots than people sometimes realize.
      ​Historically, before refrigeration, animal foods were more likely to carry
      parasites, bacteria, and foodborne pathogens.
      ​Pregnant women are more vulnerable to infections because the immune
      system shifts during pregnancy.
               ​That immune shift helps the body tolerate the fetus.
      ​Because of this, avoiding riskier foods may have offered survival
      advantages.

☆ Morning Sickness And Miscarriage Risk
      ​Nausea and vomiting in pregnancy are often associated with a lower risk of
      miscarriage.
      ​Vomiting may be linked with an even lower risk than nausea alone.
      ​The general pattern seen across research is lowest risk with vomiting,
      moderate risk with nausea only, and highest risk with no symptoms. Still, not
      having morning sickness does not automatically mean something is wrong.
               ​And, of course, this does not mean you should want worse symptoms
               for yourself. (ノω＾、) Never that! It just means those rough mornings
               are often not automatically a sign of something bad.

☆ Food Aversions During Pregnancy
      ​Food     aversions often begin during pregnancy rather than existing
      beforehand.
      ​They are usually newly developed aversions.
      ​As mentioned before, foods most often avoided include meat, fish, poultry,
      eggs, caffeinated beverages, vegetables, and alcohol.
      ​These aversions are strongest in the first trimester and usually decline
      later.

☆ Food Cravings During Pregnancy

259

      ​As mentioned in the previous section, cravings are also very common during
       pregnancy.
      ​Common cravings include fruit, fruit juice, sweets, desserts, dairy foods,
       and carbohydrate-rich foods.
      ​Cravings and aversions can sometimes act like mirror images.
             ​Foods commonly avoided may include animal products, alcohol, and
             coffee.
             ​Foods commonly craved may include fruit, sweets, and starchier foods.

☆ There May Be A Genetic Component
      ​Morning sickness may be partly heritable.
      ​Women are more likely to experience symptoms if their mother had them.
      ​They are also more likely to experience symptoms if their sisters had them.
      ​Twin patterns suggest genetics may play a role.

       ☆ Other Possible Factors
             ​Pregnancy hormones may contribute to nausea and vomiting.
             ​Smell and taste changes may also play a major role.
             ​Appetite changes, fatigue, digestion changes, and food sensitivity can
             all add to the experience.
             ​Symptoms can vary widely even when hormone levels are not clearly
             different from one woman to another.

Morning sickness is probably not caused by one single thing. It is more like a sticky
little pregnancy soup of hormones, senses, digestion, appetite, and protective
instincts!

Now for the part that tends to matter most when you are actually in it: how to
make this easier on your body! ( ◡̀_◡́)ᕤ

☆ Gentle Tips That May Help Alleviate Nausea
      ​Eat small, frequent meals instead of letting yourself get too hungry.
      ​An empty stomach can make nausea feel worse for many women.
      ​Keeping a simple snack nearby can help soften that sharp, queasy feeling.

260

      ​Bland foods are often easier to tolerate than greasy, spicy, or very rich
      foods.

☆ Foods That Are Often Easier To Tolerate
      ​Dry crackers, toast, plain rice, applesauce, or simple cereal may feel
      gentler.
      ​Fruit can be easier than heavier foods for some women.
      ​Cold foods may smell less intense than hot foods.
      ​Carbohydrate-rich foods are often more tolerable during nausea.
      ​Very strong odors can be a trigger, so simpler foods may help.

      ☆ Morning Tricks That May Help
            ​Try eating a few crackers or another dry snack before getting fully
               out of bed.
            ​Move slowly when you first wake up.
            ​Avoid jumping into a hot shower or rushing around immediately if that
               worsens symptoms.
            ​Give your stomach a softer start to the day! :-)

      ☆ Hydration Tricks
            ​Sip fluids slowly throughout the day instead of chugging large amounts
               at once.
            ​Cold water, ice chips, or diluted drinks may feel easier than
               room-temperature fluids for some women.
            ​Try drinking between meals instead of with meals if fluids make you
               feel overly full or more nauseated.
            ​Watch for signs of dehydration like dizziness, dark urine, dry mouth,
               or weakness.

      ☆ Smell-Management Tricks
            ​Avoid cooking smells when possible if they are a trigger.
            ​Open windows or use ventilation if kitchen odors make symptoms
               worse.
            ​Ask someone else to cook when you can.

261

            ​Cold meals or room-temperature foods may be easier because they
             release less smell.
            ​Strong perfumes, candles, or cleaning-product scents may also need a
             temporary break.

      ☆ Food-Avoidance Tricks (That Are Actually Helpful)
            ​If a food makes you feel intensely nauseated, do not force it just
             because it is “healthy.”
            ​Find a gentler substitute instead.
            ​If eggs are unbearable, maybe yogurt, beans, or another protein
             source feels more manageable.
            ​If meat is impossible, start with what you can tolerate and build from
             there.

☆ Ginger And Simple Nausea-Soothing Ideas
      ​Ginger is commonly used to help settle nausea and may feel soothing for
      some women.
      ​Ginger tea, ginger candies, or ginger in food may be worth trying if your
      body tolerates it.
      ​Plain, mild foods may be better than heavily seasoned foods when nausea is
      strong.
      ​Some women also do better with tart or sour flavors, though that varies.

☆ Rest And Pacing Matter More Than People Think
      ​Fatigue can make nausea feel worse.
      ​Try to rest when you can and avoid pushing yourself too hard if symptoms
      are flaring.
      ​Moving slowly, sitting upright after meals, and pacing your day may help
      reduce that overwhelmed, sick feeling.
      ​Sometimes feeling “worse for no reason” is really feeling worse because your
      body is exhausted.

☆ When Symptoms May Need More Attention
      ​If you cannot keep food or fluids down.

262

      ​If you are losing weight.
      ​If you feel faint, weak, or dehydrated.
      ​If vomiting is frequent or severe.
      ​If nausea is interfering so much that daily functioning feels impossible.

☆ The Biggest Practical Takeaway
      ​Eat before you get overly hungry.
      ​Sip fluids steadily.
      ​Avoid strong triggers.
      ​Choose gentle foods without guilt.
      ​Rest when you can.
      ​Ask for help if symptoms are becoming hard to manage.


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Morning sickness can be draining, messy, and very humbling, but it is also incredibly
common and often closely linked to the earliest, most delicate stage of pregnancy!
For many women, it may reflect the body’s effort to protect the embryo during a
vulnerable window. The best approach is a soft one: gentle food, gentle pacing,
gentle hydration, and gentle self-talk. :-) You do not have to handle it perfectly.
You just have to support yourself through it, one small step at a time.

Herbal Remedies For Pregnancy
Herbs can feel soft, natural, and comforting, especially during pregnancy, when so
many women are looking for gentler ways to manage nausea, sleep trouble, stress,
or digestion. I mean hey, who does not love a cozy cup of warm cinnamon tea with a
little swirl of brown sugar? (ᵕ—ᴗ—) No? Just me?


But, as with all things in life, there’s a catch. A big one at that. “Natural” does not
automatically mean harmless. Herbs contain active compounds that can affect the
body in real, medicine-like ways, which is exactly why they can sometimes help and
why they can also cause problems.


Some herbs are commonly used in pregnancy with more reassuring safety
information when used in appropriate forms and amounts. Others may stimulate the
uterus, affect hormones, increase bleeding risk, or potentially harm the baby. So,
stay informed, keep things simple, and run herbs, teas, tinctures, powders,
capsules, supplements, and essential oils by your healthcare provider before using
them in pregnancy. And, as always, this section is for education only, not medical
advice.

264


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

A lot of women assume herbs are automatically gentler than conventional medicine,
but pregnancy asks us to be more careful than that. In one survey of 242 pregnant
women, 9.1% reported using herbal supplements during their current pregnancy,
and 7.5% used them at least weekly. So this is not a tiny niche topic. It is
something many women are already doing. ദ്ദി(˶˃ ᵕ ˂˶)


☆ The Most Important Pregnancy Herb Rule
      ​Herbs are biologically active substances, not purposeless little leaves with
      good branding.
            ​The same property that makes an herb helpful can also make it risky.
      ​Pregnancy is not the time to casually self-prescribe concentrated herbal
      products.
      ​Always check with your healthcare provider before using herbal teas,
      capsules, tinctures, powders, extracts, or essential oils internally.
      ​Dose, timing, form, and trimester matter.

Now, let me be crystal clear: tea used occasionally is not the same thing as a
concentrated supplement taken daily! It is really a case of different format,
different impact, where the dose and delivery method make all the difference in
how your body handles it. ^___^

☆ Herbs And Remedies That Are Generally More Reassuring
      ​Some herbs and plant-based remedies have more supportive pregnancy
      safety information than others!
            ​“More reassuring” does not mean unlimited use or automatic safety
             for every person.
      ​Use the gentlest effective form, stay within common food or tea amounts
      unless your provider says otherwise, and avoid assuming more is better.

      ☆ Ginger Root
            ​Ginger is one of the best-supported herbal options for nausea and
             vomiting in early pregnancy.

265

           ​Its usefulness for morning sickness is well documented in clinical
           studies.
           ​It is considered safe in doses up to 1,000 mg per day.
           ​The risk of adverse effects at those amounts is considered low.
                   ​Easy options include ginger tea, ginger chews, fresh ginger in
                   warm water, ginger added to soups, broths, or smoothies.
           ​Small, divided amounts during the day may feel gentler than one large
           dose.

      ☆ Peppermint Leaf
           ​Peppermint leaf may help relieve nausea and morning sickness.
           ​Peppermint tea is generally considered safe in pregnancy.
                   ​The main concern is concentrated peppermint oil, especially in
                   large doses.
           ​Large medicinal amounts of peppermint oil may stimulate menstruation
           and should be avoided.
                   ​Choose   peppermint tea rather than essential oil taken
                   internally.
           ​Sip slowly if strong mint flavors worsen reflux.

      ☆ Red Raspberry Leaf
           ​Red raspberry leaf is traditionally used as a uterine tonic.
           ​Research suggests it may help tone uterine muscles.
           ​Some studies suggest it may be linked with shorter, less complicated
           labor and fewer interventions.
           ​It should be used with caution until the third trimester because of
           concern about stimulating contractions too early.
           ​Be extra cautious if you have a history of preterm labor, cervical
           issues, contractions, or a high-risk pregnancy.

      ☆ Garlic
           ​Garlic is a food-based herb with vitamin C, vitamin B6, manganese,
           and selenium.

266

                   ​Some studies suggest it may help with blood pressure and may
                   reduce risk of preeclampsia, spontaneous preterm delivery, and
                   infection.
           ​It is considered safe when consumed in normal food amounts.
           ​A common food-level example would be around one to two cloves per
           day.
           ​Avoid high-dose garlic supplements unless your provider approves
           them.
                   ​Mention it to your provider if you have bleeding issues or are
                   using other products that affect clotting.

      ☆ Chamomile Tea
           ​Chamomile tea may help with nausea and sleeplessness.
           ​It also contains calcium and magnesium.
           ​The concern is specifically with Roman chamomile in medicinal
           amounts, which is considered unsafe.
           ​Stick to simple tea amounts rather than medicinal-strength products.
           ​Double-check labels if you are buying blends, because herbal mixes
           often include other ingredients.

      ☆ Pumpkin Seeds
           ​Pumpkin seeds are more of a pregnancy-supportive food than a classic
           herbal remedy, but they still belong in this conversation! ( - ‿ - )
           ​They are rich in protein, fiber, iron, zinc, magnesium, and omega-3
           fatty acids.
           ​These nutrients support fetal development and may help reduce
           common pregnancy issues like anemia and constipation.
           ​They can be eaten raw, roasted, or sprinkled onto salads, yogurt,
           oatmeal, or smoothies.

      ☆ Slippery Elm Bark
           ​Slippery elm bark, specifically the inner bark used orally in food-like
           amounts, may help relieve nausea, heartburn, and vaginal irritation.
           ​The emphasis here is on the inner bark and modest oral use.

267

            ​As with all herbs in pregnancy, provider approval still matters!
            ​Check product labels carefully so you know exactly what form you are
             taking.
            ​Stop and ask for guidance if symptoms worsen or if you are relying on
             it heavily.

      ☆ Oats And Oat Straw
            ​Oats and oat straw are rich in calcium and magnesium.
            ​They may help with anxiety, restlessness, and irritated skin.
            ​They fit nicely into the gentler, nourishment-based category.
            ​Oatmeal can be a steady, soothing snack or breakfast.
            ​Oatmeal baths may also help calm irritated or dry skin.

      ☆ Nettle Leaf, Specifically Leaf Not Root
            ​Nettle leaf tea, not nettle root, is the form mentioned as more
             reassuring.
            ​It is rich in vitamin A, vitamin C, and vitamin K, plus calcium,
             potassium, and iron.
            ​The distinction between leaf and root matters.
            ​Use it as a tea only after checking with your provider.
            ​Be careful with mixed herbal blends that contain multiple additional
             herbs!
            ​Treat nettle leaf tea as a supportive add-on, not as a replacement for
             prenatal nutrition or iron management.

Now for the other side of the conversation: some herbs are better placed in the
“absolutely not on your own” category because they may stimulate contractions,
affect fetal development, increase bleeding, or cause other serious problems. So,
to keep things safe and sound, here are a few herbs you’ll want to skip for now
unless your provider gives you the green light:
            ​Blue cohosh.
            ​Black cohosh.
            ​Pennyroyal.
            ​Yellow dock.

268

      ​Dong quai.
      ​St. John’s wort.
      ​Saw palmetto.
      ​Goldenseal.
      ​Ginseng.
      ​Oral aloe, especially aloe latex.
      ​Ephedra.
      ​Yohimbe.
      ​Pau d’arco.
      ​Passion flower.
      ​Roman chamomile in medicinal amounts.

      ☆ Why These Herbs Raise Concern


            ​Blue cohosh contains powerful uterine stimulants and has been
             associated with fetal heart problems, stroke, and heart attack
             in newborns.


            ​Black cohosh can stimulate contractions prematurely and is
             best avoided unless medically recommended in a labor-related
             context.


            ​Pennyroyal essential oil is highly toxic, can cause liver damage,
             and may increase miscarriage risk.



            ​Yellow dock has strong laxative effects that can cause
             significant cramping and may stimulate uterine contractions.


            ​Dong quai can affect uterine activity and may increase
             miscarriage risk.

269

                  ​St. John’s wort may affect fetal development, especially in the
                   first trimester, and can interfere with medications.


                  ​Saw palmetto has hormonal activity and may interfere with
                   pregnancy-related hormones.



                  ​Goldenseal contains berberine, which can cross the placenta,
                   may contribute to kernicterus in newborns, and may cause
                   uterine contractions.


                  ​Ginseng has hormonal effects, and ginsenoside Rb1 has raised
                   concern about possible birth-defect risk.


                  ​Oral aloe, especially aloe latex, can cause strong laxative
                   effects, uterine contractions, and severe dehydration.


                  ​Ephedra and yohimbe are stimulants and are considered unsafe
                   during pregnancy.


                  ​Pau d’arco may induce uterine contractions in large oral doses
                   and may have blood-thinning effects.


                  ​Passion flower may have uterine-stimulating effects, and human
                   pregnancy safety data are insufficient.


                  ​Roman chamomile in medicinal amounts is believed to increase
                   miscarriage risk.


Now, herbal treatments come in all shapes and sizes! The exact plant part,
preparation, and dose can completely change the safety conversation. (๑´>᎑<)~
      ​Topical use and oral use are not the same thing.
      ​Food amounts and supplement amounts are not the same thing.
      ​Tea and tincture are not the same thing.

270

      ​Leaf and root are not always the same thing.
      ​Occasional use and daily use are not the same thing.

☆ The Safest Practical Approach To Herbs In Pregnancy
      ​Use food first, when possible.
      ​Use simple teas before concentrated capsules, tinctures, powders, or
      extracts, but only with provider approval.
      ​Avoid multi-herb blends when you do not fully know every ingredient.
      ​Read labels carefully, because “pregnancy tea” on the front does not
      guarantee safety.
      ​Be especially cautious in the first trimester, when early development is most
      sensitive.

☆ Tips And Tricks For Choosing Herbs More Safely
      ​Bring the exact product name or a photo of the label to your prenatal
      appointment.
      ​Ask about the herb, dose, form, and trimester, not just whether the
      ingredient sounds familiar.
      ​Avoid essential oils taken internally.
      ​Avoid trying several remedies at once, because then you cannot tell what is
      helping or hurting.
      ​Stop using a product and contact your provider if you notice cramping,
      dizziness, rash, worsening nausea, diarrhea, palpitations, or anything that
      feels off.

      ☆ A Good Pregnancy Herb Checklist
            ​What exactly is the herb?
            ​What form is it in: tea, capsule, tincture, oil, extract, powder, or
             food?
            ​How much am I taking?
            ​How often am I taking it?
            ​What trimester am I in?
            ​Does it affect the uterus, hormones, blood pressure, clotting, or
             hydration?

271

            ​Has my healthcare provider cleared this specific product?

      ☆ Biggest Pregnancy Herb Mistakes To Avoid
            ​Assuming natural means safe.
            ​Using concentrated oils internally.
            ​Starting red raspberry leaf too early.
            ​Confusing nettle leaf with nettle root.
            ​Using aloe orally because topical aloe was fine.
            ​Taking blends with ingredients you have not individually checked.
            ​Using herbs to self-manage serious symptoms instead of calling your
             provider.


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Herbs in pregnancy are not a simple yes-or-no category. Some can be gently
helpful, especially for things like nausea or mild discomfort, while others have
enough risk that they belong firmly on the avoid list unless a medical professional
is guiding their use. The safest mindset is calm, informed, and specific: keep it
simple, check every ingredient, respect the power of plant compounds, and never
feel silly for asking before you sip, swallow, or supplement. ♡.°

Pregnancy Exercises For Back Pain
Pregnancy back pain and pelvic pain can kick up quite a fuss! (╥ ‸ ╥) Standing at the
sink, turning over in bed, getting up from a chair, taking a walk that used to feel
easy … suddenly the simple things are a weight on your shoulders that you
definitely did not sign up for. Yeesh, pregnancy really knows how to throw a
curveball!

The good news is that non-strenuous exercise can alleviate some of this! (˶˃ ∇ ˂˶)
Now, it does not have to be intense, over-the-top, or exhausting to be useful.
For many women, the objective during pregnancy is not peak fitness. It is support,
comfort, and helping the body stay a little steadier through all the shifting weight,
posture changes, and muscle demands that come with growing a baby.

And, as always, this section is for education only, not medical advice. Please
check with your healthcare provider before starting or changing an exercise
routine, especially if your pregnancy is not uncomplicated or if you have pain,
bladder issues, bowel issues, dizziness, bleeding, or contractions.

275


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Pregnancy exercise is meant to support the body, not strain it. Regular moderate
movement can help with sleep, circulation, posture, and day-to-day comfort, and it
may also help reduce the risk of gestational diabetes and hypertension. When back
pain shows up, the answer is not just “grinning and bearing it.” More often, it is
gentler, smarter movement. (ദ്ദി ◠ ‿ ◠ )

So, you are probably curious as to just how much exercise you are actually
supposed to be getting right now. Well, here is your answer ( ＾ ◡ ＾ )っ:
      ​Pregnant women with uncomplicated pregnancies are generally advised to aim
      for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week.
      ​A simple way to picture moderate intensity is this: you can still carry on a
      conversation, but you are too breathless to sing.
      ​That can look like 30 minutes on most days of the week.
      ​It can also be broken into smaller chunks, like 10-minute sessions throughout
      the day.
            ​If 30 minutes feels like too much at once, shorter sessions still
             count.

You know, many women tend to think exercise only counts if it is long and
impressive. During pregnancy, consistency matters much more than a singular
grand performance.

☆ Why Gentle Exercise Can Help Back And Pelvic Pain
      ​Pregnancy changes posture, center of gravity, and the way the core and
      pelvis have to work.
            ​As the belly grows, the low back and pelvic area often take on more
             strain.
            ​Gentle exercise can help support the core, hips, glutes, and pelvic
             floor.
            ​It can also improve posture, circulation, flexibility, and body
             awareness.

276

                   ​For many women, stronger support muscles often mean less
                    pulling, less aching, and better stability!

This is why the right exercises can feel so relieving! They help distribute work
more evenly instead of letting the low back do everything by itself. Having said
that, let’s jump right into the actual exercises and have a little chat about why
they are so helpful! ヽ( > ∀ < ☆ )ノ
      ​Walking is one of the simplest and most pregnancy-friendly exercise choices.
      ​Swimming can feel especially good because the water supports body weight
      and eases joint pressure.
      ​Stationary biking is usually a safer choice than outdoor cycling because it
      lowers fall risk.
      ​Low-impact movement such as prenatal yoga, modified dance, and prenatal
      Pilates can also be great options.
            ​The best exercise is usually the one that feels sustainable, safe, and
             kind to your body!

Now, as always, safety is key! Pregnancy is not the time to go for a personal best
or prove how tough you are. It is all about finding that sweet spot where you are
staying active in a way that actually feels good for you. ᕙ( •̀ ᗜ •́ )ᕗ
      ​Always talk to your healthcare provider before starting or continuing
      exercise during pregnancy.

      ​Drink water before, during, and after movement.
      ​Wear loose, breathable clothing.
      ​Avoid exercising in very hot or humid conditions.
      ​Do not push to exhaustion.
      ​If you cannot comfortably hold a conversation, slow down.

            ​Dizziness.
            ​Faintness.
            ​Chest pain.
            ​Shortness of breath that feels concerning.
            ​Headache that does not feel normal.
            ​Vaginal bleeding.
            ​Contractions.
            ​Pain that worsens instead of easing.
            ​Fluid leaking from vagina.
            ​Anything that simply feels off to you.

      ☆ Exercises And Activities To Avoid

            ​Activities with a high risk of falling, such as downhill skiing or

            ​High-impact movement if it feels jarring or unstable.
            ​Exercises involving long periods flat on the back after the first
             trimester.
            ​Deep twisting or excessive stretching.
            ​Heavy lifting that forces you to strain or bear down.

☆ Tips And Tricks To Actually Alleviate Back And Pelvic Pain
      ​Start with a short walk if your back feels stiff rather than jumping into
      intense exercise.
      ​Use pelvic tilts and quadruped cat on days when the low back feels tight.
            ​Focus on glute and hip strength, because weak hips often leave the
             pelvis and back doing extra work.
      ​Choose side-lying or hands-and-knees positions when standing feels tiring.
      ​Use a pillow for support during side-lying exercises.
      ​Keep movements slow and controlled instead of big and dramatic.
      ​Stay hydrated, because dehydration can make the body feel worse overall.
      ​Spread exercise out through the week instead of doing too much at once.
      ​Stop before you feel wiped out.
            ​If pelvic pain, bladder issues, bowel issues, or pain with certain
             movements keep showing up, please ask for a referral to a pelvic floor
             or pregnancy-informed physical therapist. ♡


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Gentle exercise during pregnancy is not about going the extra mile. It is about
helping your body feel steadier, stronger, and a little more comfortable inside a
season of so much change. When movement is chosen carefully, modified wisely,
and done with consistency instead of intensity, it can ease back pain, support the
pelvis, and make daily life feel more manageable. Less strain, more support, and a
body that feels cared for every step of the way is all you need! (⸝⸝> ᴗ•⸝⸝)

evening habits can make a real difference in how comfortable your nights feel. And
if sleep still feels a little hectic sometimes, that does not mean you are doing
anything wrong.

Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Pregnancy sleep struggles are not some personal fail; it is just that your body is
currently doing a lot! The belly gets heavier, bathroom trips become more
frequent, heartburn can show up uninvited, and getting comfortable can start to
feel like rocket science. (⇀‸↼‶) That is exactly why practical sleep support
matters so much.

Alright, let’s kick things off with the gold standard for how to actually position
yourself for sleep while you’re expecting!

☆ The Best Sleep Position During Pregnancy
      ​The most recommended sleep position is SOS, which means sleeping on your
      side.
              ​The left side is especially encouraged because it may improve
              circulation to the placenta and baby.
              ​Left-side sleeping may also help reduce swelling, varicose veins, and
              hemorrhoids.
                    ​So, yes, left-side sleeping is golden! However either side can
                     be okay if your provider has not told you otherwise.
      ​Side sleeping generally becomes more important as pregnancy progresses
      and the belly gets heavier!
      ​This does not mean you need to panic if you shift positions in your sleep.

      Many pregnant women wake up worried because they rolled onto their back.
      Usually, the helpful response is simple: just roll gently back onto your side
      and go back to sleep.
              ​Waking up on your back sometimes is actually common!
              ​You do not need to spiral or assume you harmed your baby because you
              changed positions in your sleep.
              ​The practical move is just to reposition onto your side again.
              ​Stressing yourself fully awake over it usually helps less than calmly
              adjusting and resting.

287

☆ Pillows Can Make All The Difference
      ​Put a pillow under your belly for extra tummy support.
      ​Put another pillow between your knees to reduce pressure on the hips and
      lower back.
      ​If your back feels strained, extra side support can help keep the body more
      aligned.
      ​If heartburn is an issue, try using another pillow to raise your upper body
      slightly.
      ​A pregnancy pillow can also be a very worthwhile investment if regular
      pillows are not cutting it anymore!

Now, here’s the lowdown on making your bed feel a bit less like a battlefield and a
lot more like a sanctuary!
      ​Aim for a position that keeps the belly, hips, and back supported at the same
      time.
      ​Keep pillows nearby so you can readjust easily in the middle of the night.
      ​Use gentle support rather than forcing your body into one stiff position.
      ​If one setup stops working as your pregnancy changes, simply adjust it!
      There is no shame in this game. ( ,, > ﹏ < ,, )
              ​Comfort needs can shift week to week, and that is normal.

      ☆ Cut Back On Nighttime Bathroom Disruption

              ​Try reducing fluids a couple of hours before bedtime so you are not
              up quite as often overnight.
              ​Do not cut hydration too aggressively, though, because you still
              need good fluid intake overall!
              ​The idea is to shift more of your drinking earlier in the day, not

Safe S kincare For Pregnancy
Pregnancy can truly make your skin feel like it suddenly has a personality of its
own. ( @ __ @ ) One week it is reflective like a mirror, the next week it is breaking
out, looking more pigmented, or growing hair in places that were previously minding
their own business. That shift is very real, and it mostly comes from the hormonal
and physiological changes of pregnancy, especially higher androgen levels.

The reassuring part is that most topical skincare products are considered safe
during pregnancy because they mainly work on the surface of the skin and only tiny
amounts are absorbed into the bloodstream. So no, pregnancy does not mean you
have to give up caring for your skin entirely. It just means being a little more
thoughtful about what deserves a yes, what deserves a maybe, and what is better
left alone for now! >___<

And, as always, this section is for education only, not medical advice.

292


Main Content ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

A helpful way to think about pregnancy skincare is this: most products stay mostly
local, but a few deserve extra caution because they are absorbed more easily or
come with more concerning safety questions. So, believe me when I say that you do
not have to hyperanalyze every serum and hand cream you come across. ( _ _ )/
All you really need are a few strategic adjustments, and you will be all set!

So, why is your skin acting all brand new all of a sudden?
      ​Pregnancy causes hormonal and physiological changes in the body.
      ​Increased androgen levels can make some skin issues appear for the first
      time or become more noticeable.
      ​Common changes can include acne vulgaris, increased hair growth, and
      pigmentation shifts.
      ​Many pregnant women therefore reach for topical skincare or cosmetic
      products to manage these changes.

Additionally, it is important to note that wanting to feel comfortable in your skin
while pregnant is not vanity. It is simply part of caring for yourself. ⊹ ˚ . ♡

☆ The Big Safety Picture
      ​Most topical skincare products act locally on the skin.
      ​Because of that, systemic absorption is usually minimal.
      ​Minimal systemic absorption means very little reaches the bloodstream.
      ​If very little reaches the bloodstream, very little is likely to reach the
      fetus.
      ​This is why most common topical skincare products are considered safe
      during pregnancy.


      ☆ The Two Main Products That Need More Caution
            ​Hydroquinone should be minimized during pregnancy.
            ​Topical retinoids, such as tretinoin, are generally best avoided during
               pregnancy.

293

               ​These two stand out more than most other topical products not
               because every use causes harm, but because the caution level is simply
               higher than with most other ingredients.

So, if you remember only one thing from this section, let it be this: most topical
skincare is okay, but hydroquinone and retinoids are the big pause-and-rethink
ingredients.

Okay, now that we have cleared the air on the “doom and gloom”, let us get into the
more reassuring side of the list. ദ്ദി(ᵔᗜᵔ)
      ​Benzoyl peroxide is commonly used for acne and is considered low concern in
       pregnancy.
               ​Only a small amount is absorbed through the skin.
                     ​It is metabolized into benzoic acid and then eliminated in the
                      urine.
      ​Topical clindamycin is considered safe in pregnancy.
      ​Topical erythromycin is also considered safe in pregnancy.

       ☆ Benzoyl Peroxide
               ​Benzoyl peroxide is a common acne treatment.
                     ​About 5% is absorbed through the skin.
                     ​Once absorbed, it is converted into benzoic acid and cleared
                      from the body.
               ​Systemic effects are considered unlikely.
               ​Its use during pregnancy is not generally considered concerning.

       So if your skin likes benzoyl peroxide, this is one of the more reassuring
       acne ingredients on the list.

       ☆ Topical Antibiotics For Acne
               ​Common examples include clindamycin and erythromycin.
               ​A study involving 647 pregnant women found no increased risk of
               malformations with topical clindamycin.
                     ​Oral clindamycin studies also do not show increased adverse
                      pregnancy outcomes.

294

           ​Erythromycin has been studied in thousands of pregnancies.
           ​No teratogenic effects, meaning no birth-defect-causing effects,
            have been shown in those studies.
           ​These topical antibiotics are considered safe in pregnancy.

      ☆ Salicylic Acid
           ​Salicylic acid is found in many acne products and exfoliating products.
                 ​Absorption can range from undetectable to around 25%.
                 ​How much is absorbed depends on product concentration, skin
                  condition, pH, and how much is applied.
           ​Even so, topical use is still thought to create low systemic exposure in
            most cosmetic situations.
           ​Studies of low-dose aspirin during pregnancy did not show increased
            risk of birth defects, preterm birth, or low birth weight.
           ​Because topical absorption is much lower than oral exposure, fetal risk
            from normal cosmetic use is considered unlikely.

            This is one of those ingredients where moderation is key. A
            small-area acne treatment is a very different situation from coating
            large portions of the body in a strong peel!

      ☆ Glycolic Acid
           ​Glycolic acid is an alpha hydroxy acid, or AHA.
                 ​It is commonly used for exfoliation and acne support.
                         ​Up to 27% can be absorbed into the skin, but systemic
                          exposure remains very low with cosmetic use.
           ​Animal studies only showed problems at doses far higher than
            ordinary skincare use.
           ​With normal topical cosmetic use, glycolic acid is considered unlikely
            to pose a risk during pregnancy.

      ☆ Sunscreen (Your Best Friend (⸝⸝ ♡﹏♡⸝⸝) )
           ​Common sunscreen ingredients include avobenzone, octinoxate, and
            oxybenzone.

295

                  ​Dermal absorption is very limited.
                            ​Systemic exposure is low.
           ​No adverse pregnancy effects have been reported from sunscreen
           use.
           ​Sunscreen is generally recommended during pregnancy, especially
           because it can help prevent melasma from worsening.
           ​They are especially helpful for preventing melasma from getting
           worse.

      ☆ Self-Tanning Products
           ​Self-tanners usually contain dihydroxyacetone.
                  ​This works by binding to amino acids in the outer layer of the
                    skin.
                            ​About 0.5% becomes systemically available.
           ​That is a very low level of exposure.
           ​Self-tanning products are not expected to pose a risk during
           pregnancy.

      ☆ Hair Removal And Bleaching Products
           ​Common depilatory creams may contain thioglycolic acid.
           ​Other     ingredients    may include sodium, calcium, or potassium
           hydroxide.
           ​Bleaching products may contain hydrogen peroxide.
                  ​Hydroxide ions are naturally present in the body, and cosmetic
                    exposure is tiny compared with ordinary dietary exposure.
                            ​Hydrogen peroxide absorption is minimal and it is rapidly
                            metabolized.
           ​Topical hair removal and bleaching products are generally considered
           safe when used in moderation.

Now for the no-go list. ( ` ᴖ ´ ) This is where things get a little hazy. While the
risks may not be 100% set in stone for standard topical use, that lingering question
mark is enough for most professionals to play it safe. Since we would all rather
have a clear yes or no, the general consensus is simple: it is better to just skip
these for now.

      ☆ Topical Retinoids
            ​Topical retinoids are used for acne treatment.
            ​Tretinoin is a common example.
            ​Skin absorption is very low.
            ​However, four case reports have described birth defects that
            resembled retinoid embryopathy, the pattern associated with oral
            isotretinoin.
            ​Two prospective studies involving 96 women and 106 women did not
            find an increased risk of major malformations.
            ​Even so, the evidence is still considered controversial.
                  ​Because safer alternatives exist, topical retinoids are generally
                   avoided during pregnancy.

      ☆ Hydroquinone
            ​Hydroquinone is used to treat melasma and hyperpigmentation.
                  ​It is also found in some skin-lightening products.
                         ​This ingredient stands out because about 35% to 45% is
                            systemically absorbed.
                                 ​That is much higher than most other topical
                                  skincare ingredients.
            ​One study did not show increased adverse pregnancy outcomes, but
            the sample size was small.
            ​Because absorption is high and safety data are limited, exposure
            should be minimized during pregnancy.

☆ Tips And Tricks For Pregnancy-Safe Skincare
      ​Keep your routine simple instead of trying ten new products at once.

297

      ​Focus on gentle cleansing, moisturizing, acne control if needed, and daily
      sunscreen.
      ​Use benzoyl peroxide or pregnancy-safe topical antibiotics for acne support
      if your clinician agrees.
      ​Choose glycolic acid over stronger, more questionable actives if you want
      light exfoliation.
      ​Skip topical retinoids during pregnancy.
      ​Minimize or avoid hydroquinone during pregnancy.
      ​Wear sunscreen daily to help prevent melasma from deepening.
      ​Patch test products because pregnancy skin can become more reactive.
      ​Use hair removal and bleaching products in moderation rather than
      excessively.
      ​Ask your healthcare provider or dermatologist before using strong active
      products regularly!

      ☆ A Practical Pregnancy Skincare Routine
            ​Morning: gentle cleanser, moisturizer, sunscreen.
            ​Evening: gentle cleanser, pregnancy-safe acne treatment if needed,
             moisturizer.
                     ​For breakouts: consider benzoyl peroxide, topical clindamycin,
                     or topical erythromycin if recommended.
                     ​For pigmentation: lean heavily on sun protection rather than
                     reaching straight for hydroquinone.
                     ​For texture: a mild glycolic acid product may be a more
                     comfortable option than harsher actives.

298


Conclusion ☆ ‧ ₊ ˚

Pregnancy skincare does not need to feel like a grand undertaking. Most products
used on the skin stay mostly on the skin, which is why the overall safety picture is
much more reassuring than many women assume right off the bat. The softest and
smartest approach is to keep the basics, be cautious with hydroquinone and
retinoids, and build a routine that helps your skin feel supported without adding
unnecessary stress. Your skincare does not have to be perfect right now. It just
has to be thoughtful. ( ◜ᴗ◝ )
